platform.name: PRIMORA
platform.summary: PRIMORA is a bilingual (EN/AR, full RTL) luxury barber, beauty, spa and grooming marketplace for Saudi Arabia. Customers book appointments at provider-owned shops/branches or as home/mobile services; money is captured through Tap Payments in SAR, split into platform_share / provider_share / employee_share in transactional_ledger with ZATCA VAT, and settled to providers via payout_requests. The admin console is the only surface that can verify providers, moderate the catalog, arbitrate disputes, release provider money, and configure payment integrations.
regulatedData: Saudi VAT / ZATCA tax records (bookings.tax_amount, monthly_vat_summary)
Provider bank details: payout_requests.iban and bank_name, stored unmasked
Customer PII: profiles.first_name, last_name, email, phone_number
sourceSystems: Supabase Postgres (authoritative for bookings, ledger, payouts, catalog, identity)
Tap Payments (authoritative for charge capture and refunds; api.tap.company)
Google Maps Platform (travel time, calculate-travel function)
Unifonic / Twilio (OTP and SMS, registered but disconnected)

stack.frontend: Next.js 16.2.9 (React 19.2.4, App Router, Tailwind 4, all-client 'use client')
stack.backend: none — no Next.js route handlers, no server actions, no middleware; Supabase Edge Functions (Deno) only
stack.database: Supabase Postgres 15, SQL migrations in supabase/migrations
stack.auth: Supabase Auth (@supabase/supabase-js 2.108.1) browser client only; no @supabase/ssr, no middleware
stack.jobs: none — no queue, no scheduler, no pg_cron
stack.designSystem: Tailwind 4 utility classes, bespoke PRIMORA gold/obsidian tokens, no component library

roles.name: Platform administrator (profiles.role = admin)
responsibilities: Moderate the service catalog and pricing
Review and release provider payouts from the ledger
Configure VAT rate, commission and platform settings
scopes: platform-wide, no tenant restriction, no monetary limit
roles.authenticationStrength: email+password via Supabase Auth; no MFA, no step-up, no session-timeout policy
roles.separationOfDuties: None. Verified by security review (sec-claude-release-review): one administrator credential can edit ledger amounts directly without an audit row, originate a payout request for any provider with any IBAN, rewrite the IBAN of an existing request, approve it and release it, and can approve its own platform-setting changes. Every money command is audited with actor and reason, but nothing requires a second person. See gaps no-separation-of-duties, admin-direct-writes-to-money-tables-leave-no-audit, payout-iban-can-be-rewritten-by-an-admin-before-release and referral-and-loyalty-values-self-approved-and-unbounded.

roles.name: Provider owner (profiles.role = provider_owner)
responsibilities: Manage own shops, branches, employees and services
roles.separationOfDuties: Verified by test: an owner cannot approve or release a payout, cannot change another provider's data and cannot grant a delegated manager approval rights. Not separated: an owner approves their own supplier purchase orders, and can insert payout requests directly without the balance check (gap payout-request-insert-bypasses-balance-and-iban-checks).

roles.name: Provider employee (profiles.role = provider_employee)
roles.separationOfDuties: No financial authority. Verified by test (supabase/tests/db/admin_security_matrix.test.mjs): an employee cannot change the provider, its services or payouts, cannot insert payout requests and is refused by every administrator command.

roles.name: Customer (profiles.role = customer)
roles.separationOfDuties: Not applicable. Verified by test: a customer cannot write any table the console or the money flows use and is refused by every administrator command.

capabilities.outcome: Approve a payout request for bank processing
capabilities.rationale: Server command with a required reason and a transition matrix, behind a dialog that names the request (round 3). Built by impl-claude-release-gaps; unreviewed.
capabilities.idempotency: Repeating the same decision returns the request unchanged.
capabilities.concurrency: The payout request row is locked FOR UPDATE.
capabilities.recovery: A request moves requested -> processing or rejected only; a rejected request is final and the provider asks again.

capabilities.outcome: Reject a payout request with a reason the provider can see
capabilities.rationale: REAL BUT UNSAFE. Same path as payout.approve; the admin_note is a hardcoded English string at admin/ledger/page.tsx:582, so no operator reason is ever captured.

capabilities.outcome: Mark a payout paid and release the ledger rows that fund it
capabilities.rationale: Allocating, idempotent, reasoned release with typed-amount confirmation (round 3). Money behaviour at the bank is outside what this repository can verify. Built by impl-claude-release-gaps; unreviewed.
capabilities.idempotency: A stable key per request; the same key returns already_processed and a second key on a paid request is refused (23505).
capabilities.concurrency: The request and the ledger rows it allocates are locked FOR UPDATE; the payout is refused whole if the ledger cannot cover it.
capabilities.recovery: A payout cannot be undone from the console; the audit entry records who released it, the amount, the ledger rows and why. The amount must be typed to confirm.

capabilities.outcome: Work the queue of refund requests raised against captured payments
capabilities.rationale: /admin/refunds reads refund_requests (admin-only RLS) with server-side pagination and a status filter (impl-claude-release-gaps). Unreviewed; hosted data unverified.

capabilities.outcome: Issue a real refund through Tap and record it against the booking and ledger
capabilities.rationale: process-refund authenticates the caller (admin or scheduler), claims one refund_requests row, refunds exactly its amount through Tap with the row's idempotency key and records the result in complete_refund_request inside one transaction (impl-claude-release-gaps reassessment). Gateway behaviour unverified from this machine.
capabilities.idempotency: Each refund request carries a unique idempotency key sent to Tap; claim_refund_request only claims pending or failed rows.
capabilities.concurrency: claim_refund_request locks the row FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; complete_refund_request locks it again before writing the ledger.
capabilities.recovery: A refused refund is recorded as failed with the gateway's message and retried by the scheduler up to five attempts, then by an operator through refund.retry.

capabilities.outcome: Ask for another attempt at a refund the gateway refused, with a recorded reason
capabilities.rationale: New (impl-claude-release-gaps): admin_retry_refund_request records the operator's reason and re-opens a refund that ran out of automatic attempts for exactly one more; the screen then calls process-refund. Unreviewed.
capabilities.idempotency: The retry only adjusts the attempt counter; the money movement keeps the request's Tap idempotency key, so repeated clicks cannot refund twice.
capabilities.concurrency: The retry locks the refund row; process-refund claims it FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so a concurrent attempt is skipped.
capabilities.recovery: If the gateway refuses again the refund returns to failed with the message, and the operator decides again.

decisions.reason: The platform holds Saudi VAT/ZATCA tax records, provider IBANs, customer PII and payment references, and moves real money through Tap. ZATCA record-keeping obligations and Saudi PDPL both apply. A lower profile would let assumed decisions and missing audit pass a release gate.

decisions.decision: Archetypes are marketplace, fintech and logistics-mobility.
decisions.reason: Two-sided provider/customer marketplace; captured payments split three ways with VAT and settlement; home/mobile services with travel calculation (calculate-travel, home_services migration).

decisions.decision: Treat Postgres RLS as the platform's ONLY authorization boundary for the admin console.
decisions.reason: Verified by search: no Next.js middleware, no route handlers under src/app, no 'use server' actions anywhere in web_platform. AuthGuard is a client component that only gates rendering. Every admin read and write therefore travels from the browser to PostgREST carrying the user's own JWT, and is allowed or denied solely by RLS and is_admin().

decisions.decision: The RLS layer itself is sound and is the strongest part of the system; the defects are above it, in the UI and the edge functions.
decisions.reason: is_admin() is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, revoked from PUBLIC and anon (20260615182811:38-54). RLS is enabled on every table. The dangerous early policy 'Public read on profiles USING (true)' is explicitly dropped (:57). Column-level GRANTs stop a customer editing their own role (:75-83). Triggers protect provider control fields and validate booking transitions. Four of five views set security_invoker. Migrations use DROP POLICY IF EXISTS and are idempotent.

decisions.decision: Record which migrations are applied to the live Supabase project as UNVERIFIED, and treat 20260615182811_harden_auth_and_booking_core.sql as the single highest-stakes unknown.
decisions.reason: The Supabase MCP server is unauthenticated in this session and the live database was never queried, so no applied-migration state could be observed. If 20260615182811 is not applied, the DROP at line 57 has not run and 'Public read on profiles USING (true)' from 20260613010000_triggers_rls.sql:44 is still in force - which would make every customer name, email and phone number readable by any anonymous visitor. Every other RLS finding in this audit is conditional on that file being applied.

decisions.decision: A screen counts as REAL only when it both reads live data and surfaces a failure honestly; a screen that reports success on a failed write is classified with the decorative ones.
decisions.reason: A write path whose catch branch applies the change and reports success is operationally indistinguishable from a mock - the operator cannot tell the difference, which is the property that matters. This is why provider management, despite 1567 lines of real query code, is not treated as a working control surface.

decisions.decision: Remediation order: (1) SPINE, serialized, one implementer - harden process-refund and send-notification with the admin check from process-payout, add 'refunded' to booking_status, create admin_audit_log with append-only RLS, replace the browser payout mutation with the server function, delete the catch-and-succeed branches in provider-management, make the dev bypass opt-in. (2) TRUTH, still serialized - delete every demo fallback and render honest loading/empty/error/forbidden states. (3) FAN OUT in parallel once the spine is green - bookings detail and transitions, refund/dispute queue on payment_refund_requests, reviews moderation, employees, platform_settings for VAT and commission, real reports and exports. (4) LAST - role split and separation of duties, since it changes the RLS predicates every other slice depends on.
decisions.reason: The money and audit defects are the ones that can cause unrecoverable loss, and several share the same fix. The demo fallbacks must go before anything is verified, because while they remain no one can tell a working screen from a broken one. Role splitting is deferred to last precisely because it rewrites the authorization predicates and would force every earlier slice to be re-verified.

Auditing every landing-page load would bury the entries that matter. Proposed by the security pass; a human must confirm because it narrows the regulated-profile privileged-read rule.

gaps.description: The process-refund Edge Function performs no authentication and no authorization, acts with the service-role key, and calls the live Tap refunds API. Any caller holding the publishable key - which is committed to the repository and shipped in every browser bundle - plus a booking UUID can move real money.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: read the Authorization header, call auth.getUser, and require profiles.role='admin' exactly as supabase/functions/process-payout/index.ts:22-54 already does; restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin from '*' to the console origin.

gaps.description: Every refund path writes bookings.status='refunded', but 'refunded' is not a member of the booking_status enum, so the write always fails. In process-refund the failure happens AFTER the Tap refund has been issued, so real money leaves the account and neither the booking nor the ledger records it.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04, unreviewed): Refunds no longer touch bookings.status: they are refund_requests rows processed by process-refund (claim -> Tap with the request's idempotency key -> complete_refund_request in one transaction). REMEDY: add 'refunded' to booking_status via ALTER TYPE in a new migration, allow the transition in validate_booking_status_transition, and move the money movement and the two status writes into one SECURITY DEFINER RPC so they commit or fail together.

gaps.description: The send-notification Edge Function has no authentication and no role check and acts with the service-role key. Any caller holding the public publishable key can push an arbitrary title and body to any userId on the platform - a ready-made phishing channel against customers of a payments product.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: require a verified admin JWT before dispatch, exactly as process-payout does; rate-limit per actor.

gaps.description: Marking a payout paid runs a three-step money mutation from the browser with no transaction, no idempotency key and no confirmation: read pending ledger rows, bulk-update them to 'released', then update the payout request. A failure between the two writes leaves ledger rows released against a request that is still 'processing'; a double click releases twice. The correctly guarded server version exists and is never called.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: replace the three client writes with supabase.functions.invoke('process-payout'), then move that function's body into a single Postgres transaction (a SECURITY DEFINER RPC) and add an idempotency key on payout_request id plus attempt.

gaps.description: Roughly thirty state-changing admin commands exist and exactly three of them write an audit row. Provider approval, suspension, deletion and commission changes; ledger release; payout approval, rejection and payment; service price changes and deletions; coupon deletion; payment-method changes - all mutate silently. There is no general audit table in any migration, and the only one that exists is written best-effort inside a swallowing catch.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04, unreviewed): Every admin write to the eleven console-mutated tables is audited by trigger in the same transaction (changed fields only, sensitive values redacted, operator reason attached); every admin RPC calls write_audit_log. REMEDY: add a general admin_audit_log table (actor_id, action, entity, entity_id, before, after, reason, ip, created_at) with admin-read / no-update / no-delete RLS, write it inside the same transaction as each command, and fail the command when the audit write fails.

gaps.description: /admin/audit-logs, /admin/system-logs and /admin/webhooks all redirect to /admin/activity, which is not an audit log - it derives a feed from the six newest bookings and four newest providers and seeds hardcoded counters. The in-product help text asserts that every arbitration action is written to the audit log. An operator or an auditor asking 'who released this payout' is shown a booking feed and told it is the audit trail.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04, unreviewed): /admin/audit-logs is a real paginated, filterable view of admin_audit_logs; system-logs and webhooks now lead there instead of the booking feed. REMEDY: build a real audit-log screen over the new audit table, point the three redirects at it, and correct the help copy.

gaps.description: The VAT summary substitutes invented totals whenever monthly_vat_summary returns zero rows - not only on error - so an operator reading the platform's ZATCA tax position can be shown fabricated numbers with no indication they are not real. The same applies to provider settlement and employee earnings.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: delete every demo array; render a real empty state for zero rows and a distinct error state for a failed query. No financial screen may ever substitute invented data.

gaps.description: The VAT rate, commission rate and platform settings screens are uncontrolled inputs whose save handler only sets a success string. There is no settings table in any migration to write to. An operator can change the displayed ZATCA VAT rate, be told it saved, and change nothing - while the real 15.00 default lives in a database trigger only a migration can alter.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04, unreviewed): Taxes shows the live fee_rules the server applies (read-only by design); settings edit booking hold, loyalty and referral values only through admin_update_platform_setting, which validates, records approval and audits with a reason. REMEDY: either create a platform_settings table with admin-only RLS and wire both screens to it, or remove the screens and replace them with a read-only display of the values with a note that they are changed by migration.

gaps.description: There is no export, anonymisation, deletion or legal-hold capability for customer personal data anywhere in the console, the migrations or the edge functions, on a platform holding Saudi customer names, emails, phone numbers, booking history and private messages.
gaps.rationale: BLOCKED ON OWNER/LEGAL DECISION (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04): what a PDPL access/export or erasure request must cover (profile, bookings, invoices, messages, reviews, consents, dependents, wallet) and what ZATCA retention requires us to keep has not been decided, and AGENTS.md reserves that interpretation for a human. The console can now work a request through start, completion or refusal with the operator's own note (admin_update_data_request) and clear profile details through admin_clear_customer_profile; it no longer offers a partial JSON file as a 'PDPL export'. A real export command and a retention-aware erasure wait on the data inventory and decision recorded in pdpl-erasure-scope-undecided.

gaps.description: updateProvider, saveProvider and deleteProvider each have a catch block identical to the try block: on any failure - RLS denial, network error, missing column - the optimistic state is applied and the same success notice is shown. Provider approval, suspension, commission changes and deletion all report success whether or not anything was persisted. This also makes every authorization denial invisible.
gaps.rationale: RESOLVED in P0-C: Removed catch-and-succeed branches in updateProvider, saveProvider, and deleteProvider. Failed writes now cleanly roll back state and display honest error banners via setError(). Added server-side atomic approve_provider_application and reject_provider_application RPCs with full admin_audit_logs coverage.

gaps.description: getDevRole auto-assigns a 'customer' dev role to any visitor when none is set, and AuthGuard treats ANY dev role as authorised for EVERY dashboard including /admin. On localhost an unauthenticated stranger who loads /admin is admitted with no credentials and no click. The env flag is opt-out, not opt-in: only the exact string 'false' disables it, so 'off' or '0' leave it enabled.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04, unreviewed): Dev access is opt-in (NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_DEV_ACCESS === 'true'), never in production builds, localhost only, with no automatic role; AuthGuard admits a dev role only to its own dashboards. REMEDY: make it opt-in (enabled only when NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_DEV_ACCESS === 'true'), remove the auto-initialisation at dev-access.ts:26, require the dev role to match allowedRoles rather than granting all dashboards, and exclude the switcher from production builds. NOTE: this bypasses the UI gate only - RLS still applies - but combined with the silent-write-failure defect above, a bypassed session looks fully functional.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): getDevRole returns null in a production build and off localhost, and needs NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_DEV_ACCESS=true; no role is assigned automatically. The data stays behind row-level security.

gaps.description: The bookings screen cannot change anything. There is no detail view, no state transition, no cancellation, no no-show marking and no way to release a slot held by a booking stuck in pending_payment - even though the database explicitly permits admin transitions. Support has no lever on the platform's central entity.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04, unreviewed): The bookings console can cancel, mark no-show and complete through the existing audited booking commands, and release expired unpaid holds with a reason; status filter added. REMEDY: add /admin/bookings/[id] with audited confirm, complete, no-show and cancel commands, and a pending_payment aging queue that can release the exclusion window.

gaps.description: Disputes are synthesised from low-star reviews rather than a dispute entity. Resolving one as REFUNDED writes an enum value that cannot exist and never issues a real refund. When the underlying query fails the screen falls back to mock disputes that resolve successfully without touching the database, so an operator can believe a customer was refunded when nothing happened.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04, unreviewed): Disputes read payment_disputes and resolve through resolve_booking_dispute; no synthesized disputes or mock fallback remain. REMEDY: build the dispute queue on the existing payment_refund_requests table (which already carries a UNIQUE(ledger_id) idempotency guard), and route the refund action through a hardened process-refund.

gaps.description: Releasing a ledger payout, approving, rejecting and marking a payout paid, toggling a payment method, deactivating a branch, and permanently deleting a coupon all execute on a single click with no confirmation, no typed acknowledgement and no summary of what is about to change.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04, unreviewed): Money actions require confirmation or a typed reason (payout review, payout release, ledger release, payment methods); archive/disable actions confirm; manual phone verification confirms. REMEDY: require a confirmation dialog that names the record and the amount for every high and critical command, and a typed confirmation for irreversible money movement.

gaps.description: Every delete in the console is a hard DELETE with no soft-delete column, no archive and no restore: providers, services, coupons and integrations. Providers and services are referenced by historical bookings and ledger rows, so a delete either destroys reporting lineage or fails on a foreign key with no operator-legible message.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-04, unreviewed): Console deletes became reversible state changes: services archive (is_active false), coupons deactivate, integrations disable, provider delete removed; a test forbids admin hard deletes. REMEDY: add deleted_at soft-delete columns with RLS-filtered reads, keep hard delete for admin-only purge behind a separate audited capability, and show related-record counts before any destructive action.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): no .delete() call remains under app/admin; services and coupons deactivate (is_active=false) and say history is kept.

gaps.description: Provider bank details are stored and rendered unmasked. payout_requests.iban is selected in full and displayed in the payout queue to every admin, with no masking, no reveal-on-demand, no privileged-read logging and no field-level restriction.
gaps.rationale: BLOCKED ON OWNER DECISION: which operators may see full provider IBANs, and whether payouts need a reveal-with-reason step. Not changed by the implementer because AGENTS.md reserves sensitive-data visibility for a human. REMEDY: mask to the last four characters by default, gate full reveal behind an audited privileged-read capability, and consider column-level encryption.

gaps.description: A single 'admin' role holds catalog authority, unlimited money authority and integration-configuration authority. There is no finance role, no support role, no read-only analyst, no monetary threshold, no maker-checker on payouts and no MFA or step-up on any command. /admin/roles - which promises role administration - redirects to a decorative employees page.

gaps.description: The admin console has no Next.js middleware, no route handlers and no server actions. gaps.description: accepted_payment_methods is the only one of the five views created without WITH (security_invoker = true), and the only one granted to anon. gaps.description: Administrator RLS policies are FOR ALL on transactional_ledger, wallet_credits, gift_cards, fee_rules, customer_loyalty, loyalty_points_ledger, bookings, reviews, legal_agreements, categories, payment_refund_requests, employee_commission_rules and platform_feature_flags (and UPDATE on provider_applications), and none of those tables carries the audit trigger: trg_audit_admin_write covers only eleven other tables. Reproduction on the migrated test database: as an admin session, UPDATE transactional_ledger SET provider_share = provider_share + 5000, payout_status = 'released' WHERE id = <row> succeeds and admin_audit_logs gains no row (0 rows before and after); the same holds for fee_rules. The console's own commands are audited, but the same credential can change ledger amounts and fee percentages through one PostgREST call that leaves no trace, then raise a payout (request_provider_payout accepts is_admin at 20261005010000#L696), approve it and release it. no-audit-trail was closed for the eleven console tables only.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): the audit trigger is attached to every base table in the public schema (not to tables whose policy text mentions is_admin()), and the test enumerates the catalog, so a table without the trigger fails it. Direct changes to fee invoices, reconciliation runs and message templates are recorded; a demotion by the demoted administrator is recorded too. Issued invoices are now immutable (see the invoice gap). PREVIOUS RATIONALE: RE-OPENED BY qa-claude-release-gate (2026-10-06): the fix does not do what its rationale says. The audit trigger is attached to the tables found by pg_policies text matching ILIKE '%is_admin()%', and the test that proves coverage (security_hardening.test.mjs, 'cover every table an administrator policy can write') derives its list with the same pattern, so it cannot fail. Tables whose administrator policy is written as an inline profiles.role = 'admin' check are not covered. Reproduced: an administrator edited invoices (ZATCA tax invoices) total and VAT, deleted the invoice, changed provider_fee_invoices to paid with nothing due, flipped a psp_reconciliation_runs row from discrepant to matched and deleted it, and rewrote a WhatsApp message template, each with zero rows added to admin_audit_logs. Also unaudited: payment_disputes, notifications, provider_memberships, provider_closures, seasonal_schedules. REMEDY: derive coverage from behaviour (an administrator write to any table must add an audit row; the repro file does this per table) or attach the trigger to every table an administrator can write, and make the audit-coverage test independent of the policy text.  PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the audit trigger now covers every table an administrator policy can write (derived from pg_policies), so a direct ledger, fee-rule, wallet, gift-card or loyalty write is recorded with actor and before/after values; a test fails when an administrator-writable table has no trigger. Writing is still allowed: removing or narrowing those policies, and making ledger rows append-only, needs the owner (see admin-can-still-rewrite-money-tables-directly). REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: for every table an admin policy can write, either drop the FOR ALL admin policy to SELECT-only and perform writes through audited SECURITY DEFINER commands with a required reason (ledger, wallet credit, gift card and loyalty ledger rows should be append-only: no admin UPDATE or DELETE at all), or attach audit_admin_write and constrain the money columns with triggers so they change only through the money commands. Derive the table list from pg_policies (admin policies with cmd ALL, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE) and add a test that fails when an admin-writable table has no audit trigger. The owner must confirm which admin writes are legitimate before they are removed.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): the trigger is on every base table except the two audit logs and is derived from the catalog; behaviourally an administrator's direct write to a reconciliation run and to message templates is recorded and a customer's write is not; dropping the trigger from a table fails the test. Coverage is closed. A separate defect in WHAT the trigger records is filed as audit-redaction-is-a-short-deny-list (re-opened, high) and bulk-administrator-writes-write-one-audit-row-per-affected-row.

gaps.description: audit_admin_write redacts only seven column names (iban, api_key, phone_number, email, contact_phone, contact_email, national_id). On profiles it therefore copies first_name, last_name, gender and expo_push_token, before and after, into admin_audit_logs. Reproduction: give a customer first_name 'Sara', last_name 'Alharbi', gender 'female' and a push token, then run admin_clear_customer_profile(<id>, 'PDPL erasure request 77'); the profiles.update audit row holds first_name.before 'Sara', last_name.before 'Alharbi', gender.before 'female' and the push token in clear. The audit table is append-only, so the command that exists to clear personal details preserves them permanently, and the recovery text of capability customer.clear-profile ('records who cleared it ... without the removed values') is wrong. The existing test asserts only phone_number and uses profiles whose names are empty strings.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): sensitive columns (names, gender, push token, contact details, codes, free text, wathq data, addresses) are recognised by name and logged only as changed; the clear-profile command leaves none of the cleared values in the log. Audit rows written before this migration, if any, are an owner/legal question (pdpl-erasure-scope-undecided). REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: replace the deny-list with a per-table allow-list of columns that may be recorded (for profiles: role, language_preference, phone_verified), redact first_name, last_name, gender, expo_push_token and every free-text column, and extend release_controls.test.mjs to assert that no personal value appears in details after a clear. Decide with the owner and legal how audit rows already holding personal data are treated (see pdpl-erasure-scope-undecided).

gaps.description: At the regulated profile privileged reads must be audited. admin_customer_overview (customers.listed), get_admin_supply_overview and admin_record_export are audited, but the admin SELECT policies on profiles, consents, data_subject_requests, payout_requests, transactional_ledger and employees remain, so one PostgREST call returns the same data with no audit row. Reproduction: as an admin, select id, first_name, last_name, email, phone_number from profiles where role = 'customer' returns every customer and admin_audit_logs is unchanged (3 rows before and after). The console itself reads the data-requests queue, consents and payout_requests (IBAN and bank name in full) directly. Report exports are built in the browser from direct table reads and audited by a call whose row count the browser supplies (admin_record_export p_row_count), so audit-before-delivery is enforced by page code only. The IBAN masking in /admin/ledger is cosmetic because payout_requests.iban is still selected in full into the browser (see iban-unmasked-to-every-admin).
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: remove the broad admin SELECT policies on personal and bank tables and serve the console from audited SECURITY DEFINER read commands that mask by default (IBAN last four, reveal with a reason and an audit row) and page their results; build exports in a command that returns the rows and writes the audit entry in the same call so the audited count is the delivered count. If the owner accepts direct reads, record a confirmed decision naming the human approver. This does not replace the owner decision on IBAN visibility.

gaps.description: Row policies are public but not column-aware. 'Public read on verified providers' (roles public) with default column grants lets an anonymous caller holding only the publishable key read, for every verified provider, admin_notes (internal operator notes), cr_wathq_data (registry response), commission_percentage, cr_number, vat_number, trade_license_url and contact details. 'Public read on active employees' exposes every active employee's phone and email. 'Public read enabled payment methods' exposes payment_methods.admin_note and gateway_key. Reproduction on the migrated test database: after an admin saves provider notes, an anon session running select admin_notes, cr_wathq_data, commission_percentage from providers where id = <verified provider> receives them, and select name_en, phone, email from employees where is_active returns staff phone numbers and emails. The console writes provider notes (provider.notes) as internal text.
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the anonymous role can no longer read provider admin notes, registry data, commission, registration and contact columns, staff phone and email, or payment-method notes and gateway keys, and the public marketplace still works. STILL OPEN: every signed-in user (customer, provider, administrator share one database role) can read those columns of other providers and staff, because Postgres column privileges cannot tell them apart. REMEDY: move the internal columns to an administrator-only table, or serve them through administrator-only commands, and decide with the owner whether staff phone and email may be visible to signed-in customers at all.

gaps.description: is_admin() checks only profiles.role = 'admin' for auth.uid(); it does not require a multi-factor session (aal2), and supabase/config.toml enables no MFA. A stolen or phished admin password or refresh token therefore gives platform-wide authority over money, provider status, settings and customer personal data with no second factor, no recent-authentication requirement on payout release, refund retry or profile clearing, and an access token that refreshes indefinitely. The session lives in localStorage (persistSession) and the app sends no security headers (see admin-console-sends-no-browser-security-headers). no-separation-of-duties mentions MFA but is blocked on the maker-checker decision; MFA does not depend on that decision.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: enable TOTP (ideally WebAuthn) MFA in the hosted project, require auth.jwt()->>'aal' = 'aal2' inside is_admin() so every admin policy and command inherits it, require recent re-authentication for the critical commands (payout release, refund retry, profile clearing, settings), set an admin session time-box and inactivity timeout, and test with a token carrying aal1. Hosted Auth configuration was not observable from this machine.

gaps.description: claim_refund_request moves a refund to 'processing' and adds an attempt; only 'pending' and 'failed' rows can be claimed again, and admin_retry_refund_request refuses 'processing'. If process-refund dies, or complete_refund_request fails (refunds.ts throws), after Tap accepted the refund, the row stays 'processing' for ever: the console shows 'The gateway is processing this refund' with no action, money has left and the ledger is unchanged. Reproduced locally: after one claim a second claim returns claimed=false and the operator retry fails with 'A processing refund cannot be retried'. Separately refunds.ts records any thrown fetch error (timeout, connection reset) as a definite refusal, sets the row to 'failed' and lets the scheduler and the operator retry, so a refund Tap executed can be sent again; the shared idempotency key protects that only while Tap honours it (not verifiable from this machine). The dashboard counts processing refunds but never flags a stale one.
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the claim time is recorded, the dashboard counts refunds stuck in progress for over 15 minutes, and an audited operator command reopens one (the next attempt reuses the same idempotency key). STILL OPEN: network errors and timeouts are still recorded as definite refusals rather than an unknown outcome, and nothing looks the refund up at the gateway; Tap's idempotency window and refund lookup must be confirmed with the provider before retries can be trusted. ORIGINAL REMEDY: add an 'unknown' outcome that is never auto-retried; resolve unknown refunds by lookup at Tap by idempotency key or metadata.refund_request_id; show stale and unknown refunds on the dashboard.

gaps.description: payout_requests is updatable by any administrator and the row is the destination of the manual bank transfer. Reproduction: after a provider requests a payout, an admin session runs update payout_requests set iban = '<other IBAN>' where id = <request>, then admin_review_payout_request and admin_release_payout both succeed; the audit row is payout_requests.update with iban: {changed: true} (no old or new value, not even the last four), no reason, and the provider is not told. Administrators can also originate a request for any provider with any IBAN (request_provider_payout allows is_admin; a direct insert is allowed too). One credential can redirect a provider's money and the log cannot show to where. Distinct from iban-unmasked-to-every-admin and no-separation-of-duties, which are owner decisions.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): payout requests have no INSERT policy at all; request_provider_payout (owner only, balance and IBAN checked) is the only way to create one, so an administrator can neither insert a request with a foreign IBAN nor originate one through the command. The UPDATE lock from round 2 stays. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: RE-OPENED BY qa-claude-release-gate (2026-10-06): the UPDATE path is locked (trg_protect_payout_request_destination, tested), but the same outcome is still one INSERT away. The INSERT policy on payout_requests is 'is_admin() OR owner', so one administrator can insert a payout request for any provider with a bank name and IBAN the provider never supplied, then release it with admin_release_payout, which allocates the provider's pending ledger share to that request and marks it paid. Reproduced: provider with 450 SAR pending, administrator inserted a 400 SAR request with a foreign IBAN and released it (status paid, ledger allocated); the audit rows record the actor and the last four IBAN digits only. REMEDY: remove the is_admin() branch from the INSERT policy so a request can only come from request_provider_payout (owner, balance and IBAN checks), and keep the separation-of-duties decision on the blocked no-separation-of-duties gap.  PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): a trigger fixes iban, bank_name, amount and provider on a payout request once it exists, for every role except the payout function; the audit log records the last four digits of any bank account change on other tables. Administrators can still originate requests for any provider (payout-request-insert-bypasses-balance-and-iban-checks, no-separation-of-duties). REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: make iban, bank_name and amount immutable after insert (trigger) and allow a change only through a command that requires a reason, notifies the provider owner and records the old and new last four digits; stop administrators originating requests for other providers or require a second approver; include the IBAN last four in the payout.released audit event.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): payout_requests has no INSERT policy at all; administrator and owner direct inserts are refused 42501; request_provider_payout is owner-only (administrator, delegated manager with every operations permission and other owners refused), refuses a second submit when the balance is spoken for, and an owner's direct edit or delete changes 0 rows. Re-adding an administrator INSERT policy fails the test.

gaps.description: admin_update_platform_setting stamps approved_by = auth.uid() for settings flagged requires_owner_approval, so the administrator who edits a referral or loyalty value is also its approver; both settings were seeded 'disabled until the owner approves the values'. Validation only requires non-negative numbers, so one administrator can set referral_program.reward_sar or loyalty points_per_sar to any amount and enable it; every referral reward then inserts platform-funded wallet_credits for both customers, which are spendable as money. Nothing bounds the amount and nobody else approves it. Needs an owner decision on limits and on who approves; a human must decide.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: enforce maximum values in the command (reward amount, points ratio, redemption value) agreed with the owner, make approved_by a different principal than the editor (owner or a second administrator) and keep the setting disabled until that approval exists, and alert on enablement. The thresholds are a business decision and must not be chosen in code by an agent.

gaps.description: Beyond profiles, the audit writers copy values nobody reviewed. audit_inventory_catalog stores to_jsonb(OLD) and to_jsonb(NEW) of inventory_suppliers, including contact_name, contact_phone and contact_email. audit_admin_write copies integrations.webhook_url and key_masked (a webhook URL often embeds a secret token), providers.cr_wathq_data (can hold a registry owner's national id), providers.admin_notes, data_subject_requests.admin_notes and details (free text), payout_requests.bank_name and bank_reference, and get_admin_supply_overview logs the administrator's search text. Reproduction: as an admin, update integrations set webhook_url = 'https://hooks.example.test/h/abcSECRETtoken'; the audit row shows it in clear (api_key alone is redacted).
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 4, unreviewed): a buyer's name and any web address (integration base and webhook URLs, which can carry a token) are now recorded as changed without the value, even on the money and configuration tables; the allow-list is otherwise as in round 3b. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: RE-OPENED BY qa-claude-release-gate (round 4, 2026-10-06): the allow-list closes what was reproduced in round 3 (message variables with customer names, customer notes and leave reasons are recorded as changed without the text; verified by running them) but two full-value tables still put private values in the log. An administrator running generate_zatca_tax_invoice writes an invoices.insert row holding buyer_name (the customer's name), because invoices is on the full-value list; and an administrator's change of integrations.webhook_url or base_url logs both values in clear, including a token carried in the URL. Also on the full-value list and worth a column-level exclusion: invoices.buyer_vat_number, refund_requests.error_message (gateway text), psp_reconciliation_runs.notes. REMEDY: exclude buyer_name, the two URL columns and the free-text columns from the full-value tables (a table-level list needs a column-level deny inside it), and test every full-value table's text columns against a planted value.  PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3b, unreviewed): values are recorded by allow-list: numbers, booleans and nulls always; text only on the money and configuration tables or in columns named like a status, key, identifier, date or amount; every other change is recorded as changed with no value, so names, addresses, notes, leave reasons and structured payloads (message variables) never enter the log. Bank accounts keep their last four digits. Proven with a booking completion, a customer note edit and a leave-reason edit. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: RE-OPENED BY qa-claude-release-gate (round 3, 2026-10-06): the all-table audit trigger made the weakness of the name pattern reachable on every table. Reproduced: an administrator completing a booking writes a message_queue.insert audit row whose details hold the customer's first and last name, the branch address and booking links (the variables column), an administrator's direct edit of provider_customer_notes.notes copies the whole note (an allergy and a phone number) before and after, and an edit of employee_time_off.reason copies the leave reason. The pattern covers iban, phone, email, names, address, token, secret, comment and details only. Other columns that can hold private text and are not covered: messages.body, message_log.message_body, notifications.body_en and body_ar, provider_client_contacts.notes, refund_requests.reason, bookings.cancellation_reason, payment_disputes.reason, client_profiles.dob and metadata, job_posts.description. REMEDY: per-table allow-lists of columns that may be logged (an unknown column is logged as changed only), applied by the all-table trigger; the audit log is append-only and kept, so a value that enters it cannot be removed.  PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): redaction is now by column-name pattern rather than seven fixed names, so new personal or secret columns are covered when named conventionally. It is still a deny-list: a personal column with an unconventional name must be added to the pattern. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: use per-table allow-lists, redact URL query strings and tokens, and keep free-text and search text out of audit details; see audit-log-keeps-cleared-customer-name-and-push-token for the same fix on profiles.  QA-VERIFIED round 5 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing against the migrated schema): my two reproductions (invoice buyer name, webhook and base URL secrets) now pass: the pattern hides buyer, url, uri and webhook columns, only invoices.buyer_name and buyer_vat_number are hidden on money tables, and amounts, statuses and identifiers stay logged. Residual, by design and recorded on the bulk gap: the audit reason carries over within one transaction.

gaps.description: admin_audit_logs is protected only by the absence of RLS policies. anon, authenticated and service_role hold INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE at table level, there is no trigger refusing UPDATE or DELETE, and no hash chain or external copy. Reproduced locally: a service_role session can rewrite details of existing rows, and an added policy would immediately open every client role. actor_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting an account removes the actor from its history. The client roles are correctly refused today (tests added in admin_security_matrix.test.mjs).
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: revoke INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE from anon and authenticated (and UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE from service_role), add a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that raises, keep an actor snapshot instead of a nullable foreign key, and ship the log to an append-only sink; a hash chain is optional.

gaps.description: Every audit row is written inside the command's own transaction, so a command that fails or is refused leaves nothing: a non-administrator calling admin_clear_customer_profile, a stolen session probing admin commands, or a payout release that raises all produce no audit entry and no alert. verification.md requires that a failed command still records the attempt. Only the platform's own API logs, whose retention is not set by this project, would show it.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: record refused and failed administrator-command attempts (actor, command, error class, time) through a separate autonomous write or from the API layer, alert on repeated refusals from one session, and include them in the audit screen.

gaps.description: process-refund runs every database call with the service key, so refund.succeeded and refund.failed are written with actor_id NULL and actor_role service_role; the administrator who pressed Retry on the Refunds screen appears only on the earlier refund.retry_requested event. Reproduced locally: retry as an admin, claim and complete as service_role gives audit rows with actors <admin> and NULL. resolveCaller knows the administrator's id but never passes it on.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: pass the resolved operator id to claim_refund_request and complete_refund_request (service_role only) and store it as initiated_by in the audit details, or write an operator-attributed audit row in process-refund for admin callers.

gaps.description: A provider owner can INSERT into payout_requests directly: the policy checks only ownership, so the balance check and the SA-plus-22-digit IBAN check in request_provider_payout are skipped. Reproduced locally: an owner with a zero available balance inserted a 1,000,000 SAR request with an arbitrary IBAN string and it appears as 'requested'. Release is still bounded by the ledger, but the queue, the dashboard 'money at stake' figure and the approver's view are polluted and admin_review_payout_request does not validate either field. provider-payout-bypasses-balance-check was marked fixed for the edge function only.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: revoke INSERT on payout_requests from client roles (writes only through request_provider_payout) or enforce the IBAN pattern and available-balance rule in a trigger, and validate both in admin_review_payout_request.

gaps.description: approve_provider_application activates a provider immediately (status 'active', listed and able to take payments and request payouts) and promotes the applicant to provider_owner, but takes no reason, does not require the commercial registration to be verified or reviewed (cr_verification_status), and accepts an operator-chosen commission percentage argument. provider.approve is high risk; the audit entry records ids only. reject_provider_application does require a reason.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: require a reason or checklist on approval, require cr_verification_status verified or manually_reviewed before activation, ignore the commission argument (see provider-recorded-commission-display-only), and record the checks in the audit details.

gaps.description: next.config.ts defines no headers(): no Content-Security-Policy, no frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, no X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy; there is no vercel.json either. The administrator session is a bearer token kept in localStorage by the browser client, so any script injection reads it, and /admin can be framed by another site for click-jacking on one-click commands. The console's own rendering escapes values (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML in admin pages), which is why this is medium; the hosting platform may add headers, which was not observable from this machine.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): nosniff, no framing (X-Frame-Options DENY), trimmed Referer, HSTS and a Permissions-Policy that switches camera and microphone off are sent on every page. A Content-Security-Policy is not set (see no-content-security-policy). REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: add a headers() table: CSP with a nonce or hashes and no unsafe-inline for scripts, frame-ancestors 'none', nosniff, a strict Referrer-Policy and a Permissions-Policy; add a test that reads the table.

gaps.description: 20260704082805_live_demo_seed_messages.sql inserts four confirmed auth.users (three provider owners and a customer, all sharing one bcrypt hash) and three verified, active demo providers with branches into whatever database the migrations are applied to, including production. AGENTS.md keeps demo data in seed.sql, outside the release path. If the hosted project has this migration applied, real customers can find and book the demo providers and the demo owners can sign in if anyone knows the password behind the hash (the hash is the widely copied Supabase example string; 16 trivial passwords did not match it, which proves nothing about the real one). Hosted state was not observable from this machine.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: confirm on the hosted project that these users, providers and branches do not exist (or remove them with an audited migration), and move demo data to supabase/seed.sql so migrations never create accounts.

gaps.description: The shared allow-list that fronts every service-role function includes http://localhost:3000 in all environments, so a page served from a developer machine is an accepted browser origin in production; resolveCaller, send-otp and send-push compare the service key with === or !== against the bearer token instead of a constant-time comparison. Neither is exploitable without the token, and wildcard CORS is correctly absent.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: build the allow-list from APP_ORIGIN only outside development and compare secrets with a constant-time function.

gaps.description: supabase/config.toml fixes the one-time code for +966500000000 at 123456. The same phone number is the default recipient in the walk-in booking function. If this file is ever pushed to the hosted project, anyone could sign in as the account holding that number.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: remove test_otp from the committed file or move it to a local-only override that cannot be pushed, and make walk-in bookings without a phone store NULL.

gaps.description: has_active_consent(p_user_id, p_purpose) is executable by every signed-in user and answers for any user id, so a user who learns another user's id can learn whether that person consented to WhatsApp or marketing. Ids are unguessable, which is why this is low.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: restrict it to service_role or require p_user_id = auth.uid() or an administrator.

gaps.description: The provider dashboard's 'Print Salon QR Display' opens a same-origin window and calls document.write with the business name interpolated unescaped, so a name containing markup runs script in the signed-in viewer's origin and can read the session token. The name is set by the provider owner (and applicants), so the realistic victims are the owner themselves and staff who open the same dashboard. Outside the admin console but on the same origin and storage.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: build the window with DOM text nodes or escape the name before writing.

gaps.description: Views created before the console work (admin_data_subject_requests_view, admin_provider_applications_view, admin_provider_performance, employee_earnings_summary, monthly_vat_summary, provider_settlement_summary) still carry Supabase's default grants: SELECT for anon and INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE for authenticated. They are security_invoker and joins or aggregates, so row policy holds today and no data was returned to anon, but one policy change or one simple view would expose them. The two views added in this pass were correctly closed.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: REVOKE ALL on these views from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated, then GRANT SELECT to authenticated.

gaps.description: Two capabilities classified high or critical have no recorded safeguards, audit events or (for audit.search) server operation, authorization policy or test: refund.list (safeguards and auditEvents empty) and audit.search (serverOperations, authorizationPolicies, auditEvents, safeguards and tests all empty; only a page is cited). The security exit condition is that every high or critical capability carries all of them. audit.search is itself unaudited: reading the audit trail leaves no entry, and its rows can carry personal data (audit-log-keeps-cleared-customer-name-and-push-token).
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: record the RLS policy and admin check as the safeguard for refund.list and add an audited read or lower the risk with a confirmed decision; give audit.search a server operation (an audited, paged read command), its policy (Admins read audit logs), an audit event and a test that a non-administrator is refused.

gaps.description: Administrator policies are still FOR ALL on transactional_ledger, wallet_credits, gift_cards, fee_rules, loyalty tables and others. Every such write is now audited, but one credential can still change ledger amounts, fee percentages and balances, and then raise, approve and release a payout. Which of these writes are legitimate, and whether they should be append-only or need a second approver and recent re-authentication, is the owner's decision.
gaps.rationale: BLOCKED ON OWNER DECISION. REMEDY once decided: drop the FOR ALL administrator policies on ledger, wallet credit, gift card and loyalty ledger rows to SELECT, keep the writes in audited commands that require a reason, and add a second approver and aal2 step-up for payout release and fee changes (see no-separation-of-duties and admin-sessions-have-no-mfa-or-step-up).

gaps.description: The web app sends no Content-Security-Policy, so a script injected through any unescaped value runs with the administrator's session. A policy needs a tested list of every script, style, font, image, frame and payment origin the pages load.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: add a report-only Content-Security-Policy first, collect violations across the admin console, provider portal and checkout, then enforce it with nonces; the other browser security headers are already set in next.config.ts.

gaps.description: Provider edit, approve and detail dialogs declare role=dialog and aria-modal but never move focus into themselves, ignore Escape and neither trap nor restore focus. They are portalled to the end of <body>, so with the Edit button focused the dialog is reached only after every control on the page: the detail drawer's first control is tab stop 184 of 187 (measured at 1280 px). The application rejection modal has no dialog role, accessible name or aria-modal at all, and the bookings invoice overlay is a plain fixed div (963 controls stay reachable behind it, Escape does nothing). A keyboard-only operator cannot reach or leave these surfaces predictably.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): one dialog behaviour now serves the provider edit, approve, reject and detail surfaces, the invoice and every command dialog: focus moves in, Tab is trapped, Escape closes (unless a command is running), the rest of the page is inert, and focus returns to the control that opened it. The rejection dialog has a role and a name. Checked in a browser. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: build one shared modal primitive that follows the APG Dialog (Modal) pattern: focus the first field (or the dialog) on open, trap Tab, close on Escape, return focus to the trigger, mark the app root inert while open. Use it for the provider edit, approve, reject and detail surfaces and for the invoice, and keep role, name and aria-modal on every one.

gaps.description: The admin phone drawer is only translated off-screen when closed: its 25 controls stay in the tab order and the accessibility tree (24 of them were off-screen when tabbed at 375 px, so focus vanishes from view while a keyboard user tabs). Opening it leaves focus on the toggle rather than inside the drawer, Escape does not close it, it carries no dialog or modal semantics, and its name 'Mobile Navigation Drawer' is hard-coded English even in Arabic. The provider and customer phone menus use hidden/block with aria-expanded and aria-controls and do not have this defect.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): while the drawer is open the header, the desktop sidebar and the content are inert, so keyboard focus cannot leave the drawer; Escape still closes it and returns focus to the menu button, and widening the window closes it. Checked in a browser earlier for the drawer itself; the inert page behind it is covered by the guard test. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: RE-OPENED BY qa-claude-release-gate (2026-10-06): the drawer can now be opened and closed from the keyboard and Escape returns focus to the toggle (verified), but it declares role=dialog and aria-modal=true while open without trapping focus or making the rest of the page inert. Verified in the browser at 375 px: after opening it with Enter, 28 Tab presses moved focus out of the drawer onto a refund button behind it, and no element was inert. A modal that does not contain focus and does not hide the page misleads screen-reader users. REMEDY: use the same trap and inert handling as ModalOverlay (components/modal.tsx) for the drawer, or drop aria-modal and treat it as a disclosure.  PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the closed phone drawer is inert (out of the tab order and the accessibility tree), the open one is a labelled modal dialog that takes focus, closes on Escape and hands focus back to the menu button, and its name is localized. Checked in a browser at 375 px. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: render the closed drawer with the inert or hidden attribute (or unmount it), move focus into it on open, close on Escape and return focus to the toggle, trap focus while it is open, and localize the label.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): at 375 px the open drawer makes the header, sidebar and content inert; 40 Tab and 3 Shift+Tab presses stayed inside it; Escape closed it and returned focus to the menu button. The language-switch sliver is a separate open gap.

gaps.description: After a command or a page change, focus lands on <body>: refund retry (the table is swapped for the loading state), audit-log Next/Previous (the table and the pager unmount while loading, verified by pressing Enter on Next), settings Save (the whole form unmounts while the settings reload) and booking cancel/complete (the acted-on button disappears). A keyboard or screen-reader operator restarts from the top, behind 24 sidebar tab stops, after every action. The loading lines on the audit log, settings and taxes are plain paragraphs without role=status, so the wait is not announced either.
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): audit-log paging keeps the table and pager mounted (aria-disabled instead of disabled) so focus stays on the pager, Settings saves read the values back silently so the form stays mounted, loading lines on the audit log, settings and taxes are status messages, and a dialog that closed over a row that no longer exists returns focus to the main region instead of the page start. STILL OPEN: after a refund retry or a booking cancel the acted-on button is replaced by the reloaded row, so focus lands on the main region rather than on the next row. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: keep tables, pagers and forms mounted during reloads (dim them and set aria-busy) or move focus deliberately to the control, the next row or the result message; give every loading line role=status.  QA CONFIRMATION (qa-claude-release-gate, browser, keyboard only): the cause in the shared dialog is that the focused confirm button is disabled while the command runs (components/modal.tsx, disabled={busy}), so focus falls to <body> and is not restored when the command ends. After a refused refund retry (403) and a failed one (500) the active element was BODY and a further Enter went nowhere; after a successful retry and after a refused settings save it was BODY again. The dialog still traps and Tab re-enters at the reason field, so the operator is not stuck, but each command costs a keyboard user their place. REMEDY: keep the button enabled with aria-disabled while busy, or return focus to the dialog's first invalid field or to the result message when the command ends.

gaps.description: Command results (success, refusal, gateway failure) render in a banner at the top of the page. With the operator working in a long table the banner is out of sight: after cancelling the 200th booking in the list the 'Booking updated.' notice sat 37,329 px above the viewport, and on customers and providers both the success notice and the too-short-reason error were outside the viewport when the row's button was used (all verified in the browser); on a phone the Reports result line is above the fold of the card whose button was pressed. Screen readers hear role=status but sighted operators see nothing, so a failed money or PII command can look as if nothing happened.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): command results (success, refusal, gateway answer, export outcome) are shown in a message fixed to the bottom of the viewport, whichever row the operator was working in; a refusal stays until dismissed and a success clears itself. Bookings, customers, refunds, reports and providers use it; a refusal inside a dialog stays in the dialog. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: show the result next to the control (per-row message or a viewport-anchored toast), mark the changed row, or scroll to and focus the message; keep failures on screen until dismissed.

gaps.description: customer.clear-profile (risk critical in the manifest, 'not reversible by design') is confirmed by a native window.prompt whose text never names the customer: no name, email or ID, no typed confirmation of the target, and the reason is lost if the command then fails. The red button sits beside 'Remove verification' in every row, and the prompt appears detached from the row. By the console's own standard high and critical commands need typed confirmation of the target plus reason capture; here one reason of three characters erases a person's name, email, phone, gender and push token. Verified: the prompt for row 19 said only 'Reason for clearing this customer's profile details'.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): clearing profile details now opens a dialog that names the customer (name, email, phone, full ID), lists what is removed and kept, needs the first eight characters of the ID typed and the operator's reason, keeps both when the command is refused, and reports the result in a message anchored to the screen. Checked in a browser against a stand-in API: an empty submit is blocked with the fields named, a refusal keeps the typed text, success closes the dialog, restores focus and announces the result. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: replace it with a modal that states the customer's name, email and ID, lists what is removed and what is kept, requires typing the ID prefix, keeps the reason when the command fails and reports the result next to the row.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): the clear-profile dialog names the customer (name, email, phone, ID), states what is removed and kept, requires a reason of at least 3 characters and a typed confirmation (first 8 characters of the ID); an empty reason or a wrong confirmation sent no command to the stand-in; Escape returned focus to the trigger.

gaps.description: Apart from provider status changes, every operator command asks for its reason through window.prompt and the text does not identify the target: cancel and no-show do not say which booking, verify/remove phone and the three data-request actions do not say which customer or request, refund retry names only the amount (several refunds share SAR 60, 85 or 450). Provider suspend names the provider but previews nothing: the warning that upcoming bookings were not changed appears only after the status has changed, and approving an application (which creates a provider and upgrades the user role) captures no reason at all. A native prompt cannot follow the page direction, loses the typed reason when the command fails, and a browser's 'prevent additional dialogs' setting turns the buttons into silent no-ops (a null answer returns without any message).
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): every operator command in the admin console, including application approval (which now takes a reason), uses a dialog that names the target, states the consequence, captures the reason and keeps it when the command fails. STILL OPEN: the dialogs do not preview counts (upcoming bookings, money at stake) before the command is sent. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): bookings, customers, data requests, refunds and provider status changes now use a dialog that names the target, states the consequence, captures the reason and keeps it when the command fails (no native prompts remain on those screens); suspending or rejecting a provider says upcoming bookings are not changed before the command is sent. STILL OPEN: approving a provider application still captures no reason, and the dialog does not preview counts (upcoming bookings, money at stake). REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: ship one command dialog that names the target, previews consequences (upcoming bookings, refund amount and invoice, money at stake), captures the reason, keeps it on failure and reports the result; use it for application approval as well.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): the remainder is described honestly: the application approval dialog now names the applicant, both business names, contact and CR number, states what approval does, and requires a reason; no dialog previews counts or money at stake. The provider application rejection still uses its own modal and the CR review uses bare prompts (provider-registration-review-still-asks-through-bare-native-prompts).

gaps.description: The new Reopen action on a refund stuck in progress asks for a reason in a native prompt that tells the operator 'if the refund was issued, retrying with the same reference returns it instead of sending it twice'. The console states this as fact on a money command, but the manifest records the gateway's behaviour as unverified from this machine, and the prompt names neither the refund nor its amount or booking, so the operator cannot confirm which refund they are reopening while the gateway check is still pending. Rows with no claim time render as 'Stuck in progress since —'.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the reopen dialog names the refund (reference, amount, booking, request time, in-progress time or 'not recorded'), no longer states that a repeated reference is safe, says it has not been confirmed with the provider, and needs the operator to tick that they looked the refund up in the gateway. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: reword the assurance as a checklist the operator confirms (what to look for in the gateway, with the refund reference and amount shown), name the refund in a proper dialog, and show an explicit 'claim time unknown' message instead of a dash.

gaps.description: Row actions repeat one visible name with no row context, so screen-reader and voice-control operators cannot tell them apart. Measured with an accessible-name sweep: Retry now x24 on refunds; Invoice x500, Cancel x403, Complete x29 and No-show x29 on bookings; Clear profile details x24, Verify phone and Remove verification on customers; Show x50 on the audit log; View, Edit and Suspend x38 on providers; Reopen on stuck refunds. The three Download CSV buttons on Reports sit in sections with no accessible name.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): row actions on bookings, refunds, customers, data requests, the audit log, providers and reports carry a name that includes the row (for example 'Cancel booking be7b0632', 'Retry refund …, SAR 60.00'). REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: give each row action an aria-label (or aria-describedby pointing at the row's identifier cell), for example 'Retry refund #1001, SAR 60.00', and name the Reports sections with aria-labelledby.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): refund, booking and customer row actions carry the record in their accessible name (for example 'Retry refund rf-023-7, SAR 60.00', 'Cancel booking dddfe2ad', 'Clear profile details: Mohammed Al-Otaibi').

gaps.description: A 403 / permission-denied answer renders exactly like an outage: the same red banner ('... could not be loaded: permission denied for ...') with a Try again button that cannot succeed. Verified by forcing 403s on the dashboard, refunds, audit log, customers and employees. The manifest declares 'forbidden' as a covered state on each of these screens, but a revoked or downgraded operator gets a retry loop and no explanation of what access is missing or whom to ask.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): a refused request (42501, PGRST301, 401, 403, 'permission denied') shows what happened, who to ask and a way back to the dashboard, with no retry loop, on the dashboard, refunds, audit log, customers, employees, settings, taxes and bookings; outages keep the retry. Checked in a browser with a forced 403. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: map 42501, 403 and PGRST301 to a forbidden state (what access is missing, who grants it, no retry, link back to the dashboard) and keep the outage state for 5xx and network failures; then record 'forbidden' in the screens' states.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): the dashboard shows 'You do not have access to this screen' for a 403 and a separate error with Try again for a 500; a refused command inside a dialog shows the server's message and keeps the input (the message is the raw database text, for example 'permission denied for rpc:...').

gaps.description: The customer screen marks its two tabs role=tab with aria-selected inside role=tablist but defines no tabpanel, aria-controls or roving tabindex: both tabs are in the tab order and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight do nothing (verified). That promises the APG Tabs behaviour it does not deliver. On Providers the application-status chips (All, Pending, Approved, Rejected) expose no pressed state while the registry chips beside them do.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the customer view switch is now a group of pressed-state buttons rather than half of the tab pattern, and the provider application chips expose their pressed state like the registry chips. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: finish the APG Tabs pattern (tabpanel, aria-controls, arrow keys, roving tabindex) or drop the roles and use aria-pressed buttons; add aria-pressed to the application chips.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): the two sections are a labelled group of toggle buttons with aria-pressed; /admin/customers?tab=requests opens the data-request section.

gaps.description: Tailwind 4 resolves 'outline-none focus-visible:outline-2' to outline-style none, so the eight Settings inputs show no focus indicator at all, and the Provider search, sort and edit fields change only their border colour to #D1AF47 (about 2.1:1 against white, under the 3:1 non-text minimum); the rejection-reason textarea only gains a red border. Separately, the unlayered rule '.primora-dashboard-sidebar nav a[aria-current=page]' sets box-shadow and overrides the layered focus ring, so the link for the page you are on has no focus indicator. Measured by focusing every control with keyboard modality on each screen.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): no admin control hides its outline any more (settings, providers, coupons, integrations, services, ledger and notifications inputs keep a visible 2 px ring), the link for the current page shows its ring over the glow, and a guard test fails when an unprefixed outline-none is added. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: remove outline-none from the shared input classes (keep a visible outline or ring), keep the ring on the active nav link by raising its specificity or layering the rule, and re-run the focus sweep on every screen.

gaps.description: Paginated lists order by created_at alone. admin_audit_logs.created_at defaults to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (transaction time), so every audit row written by one command (the command entry plus the trigger entries) shares an identical timestamp, and refunds created in one transaction tie as well. With offset paging (50 rows per page) PostgreSQL may repeat or skip tied rows across a page boundary, and the on-screen time (seconds) cannot order them, so an auditor can miss an entry. Bookings order by scheduled_at alone over the newest 500.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): audit-log, refund and booking lists end their sort on the row ID, so rows that share a timestamp keep a stable order across page boundaries. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: append the unique id as the final sort key on every paginated query (or add a monotonically increasing sequence column to the audit table) and use it as the page cursor.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): refund, booking and audit requests order by the timestamp then id (order=created_at.desc,id.asc; scheduled_at.desc,id.asc) in the captured network log.

gaps.description: No admin screen reads or writes URL state (no useSearchParams, router.push or location.search anywhere under app/admin), so tabs, status filters, search terms and pages cannot be bookmarked, pasted into an incident channel or restored on reload, and the dashboard's drill-downs land on each screen's default view. Verified for providers: 'Provider applications to review' (4) opens the Active Providers Registry with 38 rows instead of the Applications queue. By the same routing 'Personal data requests (PDPL)' opens the customer directory rather than the data-rights tab, and 'Unpaid holds past the hold time' opens all bookings rather than pending_payment.
