gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): providers (tab, status, application status, search), customers (view, search) and bookings (status) read and write their filters in the address bar, and the dashboard queues open the exact view they count (applications, data requests, unpaid holds). Checked in a browser. STILL OPEN: the audit log, refunds and employees filters are not in the address bar yet. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: put tab, status filter, search, page and sort in the query string, read them on mount, and make each QUEUE_ROUTES entry a deep link that filters to exactly the records the count describes.

gaps.description: The filter bar combines 'flex flex-col ... lg:flex-row ...' with ${rowDir} (flex-row, or flex-row-reverse in Arabic) on the same element, and the row direction wins at phone width: the search box and the status chips share one line inside a card that clips its overflow. At 375 px in English the Pending and Suspended chips and the sort select are cut off; in Arabic all seven status chips sit outside the card (x 340-449 against a 359 px card edge) and cannot be tapped, so a phone operator cannot filter providers by status. The implementer's note records a 375 px check of this screen.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the filter bar changes direction only from the lg breakpoint, so the search box and the status chips wrap instead of being clipped. Checked in a browser at 375 px in English and Arabic: every chip sits inside the card and the page does not scroll sideways. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: apply the row direction only from lg: upward, let the chip group wrap, and re-check the screen at 375 px in both locales.

gaps.description: The global rule on '[class*=rounded][class*=border]' sets overflow:hidden (unlayered, so it beats Tailwind's layered overflow-y-auto). The invoice panel (max-h-[90vh], overflow-y-auto) therefore cannot scroll: at a 600 px-high viewport 204 px (the ZATCA QR block and the Print Invoice button) are clipped and unreachable, and at 375x812 the Print button is cut off by 37 px and sits under the dev pill. Dialogs portalled to <body> (providers) are unaffected. On phones the top bar also paints above the dim layer because the overlay lives inside main's stacking context.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): dialog panels are exempt from the card skin that forced overflow:hidden, so the invoice panel scrolls and the Print button is reachable; the invoice is portalled to the page body above the top bar. Checked in a browser. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: exempt dialog panels from the skin rule (a :not([role=dialog]) clause or a data attribute) or portal the invoice like the provider dialogs, make the panel scroll, and verify at 600 px height, 200% zoom and 375 px width.

gaps.description: Opening an invoice requests https://api.qrserver.com/v1/create-qr-code/?data=<ZATCA payload> from the operator's browser. The payload is the invoice's TLV record (seller name, VAT number, timestamp, total and VAT), so every invoice view discloses tax data and the admin's IP address to a third-party service, and the QR block is blank whenever that host is blocked or offline. Routed to the security pass as a data-exposure finding; the UX consequence is a missing QR on a legal tax document.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the invoice no longer requests a QR image from an outside service: the encoded ZATCA value is shown as text with a Copy action, and a test fails if any admin screen calls a third-party QR host. A drawn QR image needs a local encoder (see invoice-qr-image-not-drawn-locally). The provider dashboard's printable booking-page QR still uses the same outside service (a public booking URL, not tax data). REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: render the QR locally (client library or a server-generated SVG), block the third-party host with a CSP, and keep the base64 text visible as the fallback.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): opening the invoice dialog on /admin/bookings requested only localhost and the stand-in API host; no image, frame or script from another host; the payload is shown with a Copy action. (The provider dashboard's QR print window is a separate screen and is covered by qr-print-window-writes-business-name-as-html.)

gaps.description: The Taxes screen presents 'VAT 15%', 'Tips: 0%', 'If no active rule matches a booking source, the server applies 15%' and 'No municipality or service fee is added' as the rates the server applies, but they are literals in the page: none is read from a source and none is registered in declaredStatic[] with a reason and approver (the only registered static is the P3 catalog vocabulary). The VAT rate itself appears as a literal in at least nine places across the SQL migrations rather than as one setting. The commission table is live. The loading line has no role=status and the load error has no Retry button, unlike the other screens.
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the loading line is a status message and a failed read has a Try again action. STILL OPEN: the VAT 15%, 0% tips and 'no other fee' statements are still literals in the page: registering them in declaredStatic[] needs a named human approver, or the rate must come from one setting that the SQL also reads. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: register each literal in declaredStatic[] with the owner who approved it, or read the rate from one authoritative setting that the SQL also uses; add role=status to the loading line and a Retry action to the error.

gaps.description: The Reports subtitle says dates are Riyadh dates, but the VAT summary and provider settlement views group with date_trunc('month', ...) in the database session time zone (UTC unless the project overrides it), so a booking at 01:00 on the 1st in Riyadh falls into the previous month's row. The file name 'vat-summary_2026-08-15_2026-10-06.csv' also implies a half month while its rows are whole months (only the card text says months that overlap are included). For a tax export this can misstate a ZATCA period boundary.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the monthly VAT, provider settlement and employee earnings views cut months in Asia/Riyadh (tested with a booking at 01:30 Riyadh time on the 1st), the monthly files are named with the months they contain, and the card text says whole Riyadh months are included. Migration 20261005160000 is not applied to any hosted project. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: bucket in the views with AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Riyadh', write the period and time zone into the file, and reword the subtitle per report so it does not claim Riyadh dates where the data is bucketed otherwise.

gaps.description: The admin translations define langSwitch ('العربية' / 'English') but the shell never renders a control, unlike the provider and customer shells. An operator inside /admin cannot change language; it comes only from primora_lang set on another page (a fresh browser opens in English). The AR/EN rule in AGENTS.md is therefore not met for the console shell.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the sidebar footer and the phone header carry a language switch that writes the same primora_lang value and html lang/dir as the provider and customer shells. Checked in a browser: switching reloads copy, direction and the page title in Arabic with no horizontal scroll at 375 px. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: render the same toggle in the admin sidebar footer and the phone header, writing primora_lang and the html lang/dir exactly as the provider and customer shells do.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): the switch changes dir and lang and stores primora_lang; no horizontal scroll at 375 px in Arabic. A residual drawer-offset defect after switching at phone width is filed as phone-drawer-leaves-a-sliver-on-screen-after-a-language-switch.

gaps.description: The customer shell shows a hard-coded unread badge '3' on Messages and an 'AI Assistant' card reading 'I found 2 slots this week that match your routine' (English only, linking to /customer/search); the provider shell shows an always-on pink dot on Messages. None is bound to data. Both shells also have a header search box with no state, handler or form, an accessible name that is only its placeholder, and a width of 81-113 px at 375 px, so typing does nothing.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the invented unread badge, the 'AI Assistant' card and the always-on dot are gone; the Messages badge and dot are now the count of conversations with an unread message, read from conversations (nothing is shown when it cannot be read). The customer header search is a link to the real search screen and the provider shell has no search box. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: bind the badge and dot to a real unread count or remove them, delete or wire the AI card (server data, localized), and remove or implement the search inputs and give them an accessible name.

gaps.description: AuthGuard calls signOut() whenever the profile read returns any error, and every Log Out button calls signOut() with no options. In the installed @supabase/auth-js 2.108.1 the default scope is 'global', so a transient profiles error, or simply pressing Log Out, ends every session the operator holds on every device. When the sign-out request itself fails the library returns the error without clearing the local session; the layouts ignore it and still navigate to /login, so the console says logged out while the session remains in the browser. Routed to the security pass (session handling).
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): Log Out ends this device's session only (scope local) in the admin, provider and customer shells, and says so when the request fails instead of navigating away; a failed profile read in the session check is an error with a Try again button instead of a sign-out. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: sign out with scope 'local' unless the operator chooses 'sign out everywhere', treat a failed profile read as an error state with Retry rather than a sign-out, and check and report the signOut error.

gaps.description: Every admin route has the same document title ('PRIMORA - Luxury Beauty & Grooming Marketplace') because the admin layout is a client component and no page sets its own. Only the dashboard and refunds have an h1; the audit log, settings, taxes, reports, customers, employees, bookings and providers use h2 for the page title, and the first heading in the DOM on every page is the sidebar's h5 'Need Help?'. The sidebar nav has no accessible name, main has no id, there is no skip link (24 tab stops precede the content), and the AuthGuard loading text 'Verifying secure session...' is English only and not announced.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): every admin screen has its own localized document title (re-asserted after the framework sets its own) and a level-one heading, the sidebar navigation has a name, the 'Need Help?' heading is no longer the first heading, there is a skip link to a focusable main region, and the session check shows a localized status line. Checked in a browser. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: set a per-route title (server wrapper or document.title effect), make the page title the h1, label the sidebar nav, add a 'Skip to content' link to a focusable main, and localize the guard's loading line with role=status.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): every admin route sets its own localized title ('Refunds · PRIMORA Admin', 'المبالغ المستردة · إدارة PRIMORA').

gaps.description: Tables keep 760-1040 px minimum widths inside a scroll region. At 375 px the refunds table shows date, amount and source; the status column and the Retry button start at x=756 with no scroll cue (verified), so a phone operator works the refund queue without seeing status or the action. The audit log's Record, Reason and Details columns and the customers' Actions column are likewise beyond the first screen.
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the refunds table now puts the refund (amount, date, reference), its status and its action first and shows a swipe hint on phones. STILL OPEN: the audit log, customers and providers tables still scroll sideways with the key columns off screen. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: at phone width render each row as a card (identifier, status and the primary action first) or pin the identifier and status columns, and add a visible scroll cue to any table that still scrolls.

gaps.description: An audit-log date range with From after To is not validated and shows 'No entries match these filters.' (verified). Settings validation answers every bad field with 'Enter valid numbers.' without naming the field or the allowed range (the 5-120 minute rule exists only in the help text), the inputs are not marked aria-invalid and focus does not move to the error. The provider edit dialog reports one error at a time ('Both business names are required.'). The refund result notice is never cleared by a filter or page change, so a failed retry from earlier stays beside an unrelated list or load error (verified), and the filtered-empty messages on refunds, customers and employees do not offer Clear filters.
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the audit log refuses a From date after the To date with a named message, Settings names the field and the allowed range, marks the field invalid and moves focus to it, a refund notice is cleared when the view changes, and filtered-empty states on refunds, customers and employees offer a way back. STILL OPEN: the provider edit dialog still reports one error at a time. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: validate ranges inline with the field named, set aria-invalid and aria-describedby, clear stale notices on navigation, and add a Clear filters action to filtered-empty states.

gaps.description: KPI tiles outside the dashboard declare no definition, window, source or drill-down. Providers' 'Applications' tile counts providers with status pending (3 in the test data) while the Applications queue tab beside it counts 4 pending applications, and its 'Revenue' tile is all-time gross with no window. The Bookings tiles 'Total Volume' and 'Platform Revenue' are sums over the newest 500 rows only (a note says so, the tile labels do not).
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the bookings tiles are relabelled with what they cover (the listed bookings, newest 500). STILL OPEN: the providers tiles still carry no definition, window or drill-down. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: give each tile a one-line definition and window like the dashboard cards, link it to the list filtered to the same records, or remove it.

gaps.description: Booking times use toLocaleString without a timeZone, so they show in the browser's zone (an operator outside Riyadh sees different hours than the shop and the dashboard); other screens format in Asia/Riyadh but only the dashboard says so ('Times are shown in Riyadh time'). Currency is rendered four ways: 'SAR 1,250.50' and 'ر.س.' through sar(), 'ريال' in the bookings table and tiles, and a hard-coded Latin 'SAR' on the invoice inside the Arabic UI. Digits alternate between Arabic-Indic and Latin across screens (taxes and settings inputs against the dashboard).
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): bookings and the invoice now format every time in Riyadh time and every amount through the shared SAR formatter, and the page says times are Riyadh time. STILL OPEN: one numeral system per language is not yet chosen: taxes, settings and a few inputs still alternate between Arabic-Indic and Latin digits. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: route every date through operationsDate with an explicit Asia/Riyadh label, every amount through sar(), and choose one numeral system per locale.

gaps.description: The provider dropdown query on the Employees screen ignores its error (const { data } only): when it fails the filter silently offers only 'All providers' (verified with a forced 500), and the list is capped at the API's 1,000-row limit with no notice, so filtering by a provider beyond that is impossible.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): a failed provider-filter query is reported beside the filter with a Retry action, and a list that reaches the 1,000-row ceiling says so; the main list also separates a refused request from an outage and offers Clear filters when a filter matches nothing. A searchable server-side provider lookup is not built. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: surface the error beside the filter with a Retry action and replace the plain select with a searchable server-side provider lookup.

gaps.description: The Arabic sidebar label for the employee directory is 'الموظفون والصلاحيات' (Employees and permissions) and the retired /admin/roles and /admin/teams addresses redirect there, but the screen is a read-only directory with no role or permission administration. The 'Need Help? / System Support' card links to Settings rather than the Help Center or a support channel, and the Help Center is reachable only from the dashboard header.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the Arabic staff label is now 'الموظفون' (no permission management is promised) and the help card leads to the help centre. The retired /admin/roles address still redirects to the staff directory. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: rename the Arabic item to الموظفون, send /admin/roles somewhere honest (or drop the redirect), and point the help card at /admin/help.

gaps.description: Computed contrast sweeps (text over its composited background) found: the green 'Verified' badge at 3.12:1 on customers (14 rows), the 10 px grey 'ID ...' labels at 3.3:1, the grey '0' count badges on the dashboard at 2.49:1 and the gold 'SAR' and '%' glyphs at 2.0:1 on bookings, all under 4.5:1. 8-10 px text is common (sidebar section labels at 9 px, the ADMN chip at 8 px, 1,762 text nodes under 11 px on the bookings table).
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): the customer, bookings, refunds, audit-log, taxes, employees, providers and shell screens use an 11 px floor and darker badge colours (verified badge and ID labels now pass 4.5:1). STILL OPEN: the dashboard count badges and the gold SAR and % glyph contrast outside these screens were not re-measured. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: darken those badge and label colours to at least 4.5:1 and set an 11-12 px floor for operator-facing text.

gaps.description: A data request row shows the customer's name and an 8-character ID but does not link to the directory row or its Clear profile details action, so an operator working an erasure request has to switch tabs, retype the name and find the row. The related-record chain of the console standard (queue, record, action, result) is broken at this step.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): each data request row has an 'Open customer record' action that opens the directory filtered to that customer's ID (the directory search now finds a complete customer ID, tested), and the address carries the filter. Checked in a browser: the link switches view and shows exactly one row. The request row does not yet show the outcome of a profile clearing. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: link the row to the directory filtered to the customer ID (via URL state) and show the outcome of any profile clearing on the request.  QA-VERIFIED (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, stand-in API and Browser pane; not the hosted project): each data-request row has 'Open customer record: <name>' plus start, complete and refuse actions named with the request.

gaps.description: The repository's only fixtures are 2 customers, 2 providers and 2 bookings with no refund requests, audit rows, data-subject requests or consents, and the implementer's browser checks ran against a 3-provider stub. Pagination (25, 50 and 500 rows), filtered-empty, long Arabic names, null optionals, timestamp ties, failed refunds past five attempts and overdue PDPL requests cannot be reproduced from seed data, and several defects above (clipped filter bar, tie ordering, off-screen results, invoice clipping at short heights) only appeared against production-shaped data.
gaps.rationale: REMEDY: add an idempotent volume-fixture script outside the release path (more than 1,000 customers, bookings in every status, 60+ refunds in every state, 200+ audit rows sharing timestamps, long Arabic and English names, null optionals, overdue PDPL requests) and run the UX sweep against it; the generator used in this review is described in .admin-console/worklog/ux-claude-release-review.md.

gaps.description: When the bookings query fails, the page shows the reason in a plain div below the table: no role=alert (nothing is announced), no Retry button, and the table above keeps its empty 'no bookings' body rather than an error body. Verified by forcing a 500 on the bookings table: the banner exists but the page exposes no alert or status role at all, unlike the dashboard, refunds, customers and employees screens.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, unreviewed): a failed bookings read is an alert naming the reason with a Try again button, and a refused request is shown as such. REVIEWER'S ORIGINAL REMEDY: render the failure as the screen's body (role=alert, the reason, a Try again button) and hide the empty-table row while it is shown, as the refunds and customers screens do.

gaps.description: The invoice screen no longer sends the tax record to an outside service, so it shows the encoded ZATCA value as text instead of a drawn QR image. An operator cannot scan the invoice from the screen, and the provider dashboard's printable booking-page QR still uses the outside service.
gaps.rationale: BLOCKED ON A DEPENDENCY DECISION. REMEDY: draw the QR in the browser with a small encoder (toqr 0.1.1, MIT, is already in the lockfile through the Expo CLI) or generate an SVG on the server; adding a direct dependency changes package.json and the lockfile, so it needs the owner's approval; verify by scanning the result with a ZATCA-capable reader.

gaps.description: A provider owner (or a delegated booking manager) can change a booking's status with a direct table write instead of the commands. Cancelling a paid booking this way creates no refund request, leaves cancelled_by empty, and the customer's deposit stays in the ledger as pending payout to the provider; cancel_booking() would have created a refund for the full deposit. Completing or marking no-show a booking that has not started is refused by employee_update_booking_status and mark_booking_no_show ('cannot be completed before its start time') but accepted on the direct path, and completion fires trigger_on_booking_completed_rewards (loyalty points, referral wallet credits, gift-card and platform-discount settlement rows payable to the provider). The status-transition trigger only checks who may move which state, not the preconditions the commands enforce.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): the provider-owner and delegate UPDATE policies on bookings are dropped, so a status can only change through cancel_booking, mark_booking_no_show and employee_update_booking_status (which refuse an unstarted booking and create the refund). The provider calendar now cancels through cancel_booking. Proven: a direct cancel, completion and no-show change zero rows, the command still refunds the full deposit. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate, reproduced against the migrated schema (PGlite): owner1 'update bookings set status = cancelled' on a confirmed paid booking returned 1 row, refund_requests count stayed 0, ledger payout_status stayed pending; the same owner calling cancel_booking() produced a refund of the full deposit (17.00). Direct 'completed' and 'no_show' updates on a booking 3 days in the future succeeded while the commands refused. REMEDY: remove the owner and delegate UPDATE policies on bookings.status (or drop UPDATE on bookings for non-admin roles entirely) and let cancel_booking, mark_booking_no_show and employee_update_booking_status be the only path; keep validate_booking_status_transition as defence in depth and have it enforce the same preconditions (start time, refund creation). Not an admin-console screen defect: it is the database authorization boundary the console relies on.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): bookings keeps one write policy, the administrator's (catalog check); owner, assigned employee, customer and other owner changing status, check-in time or deleting the booking change 0 rows and no refund is created; the commands still work for the owner; no web, mobile or edge-function code writes a booking directly (every from('bookings') is a read). Mutation: restoring an owner UPDATE policy fails the test. Admin direct writes remain possible by design and are audited (see admin-can-still-rewrite-money-tables-directly).

gaps.description: The invoices table (ZATCA tax invoices, hash-chained by invoice_hash and previous_invoice_hash) has an administrator FOR ALL policy and no immutability trigger. An administrator can change total_amount_sar and vat_amount_sar or delete an issued invoice with one write; the stored invoice_hash and zatca_qr_code then no longer match the document, and nothing is recorded (see admin-direct-writes-to-money-tables-leave-no-audit).
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): administrators only read invoices (the FOR ALL policy is gone) and a trigger refuses any change to an issued invoice's figures, hash, QR value or seller and any delete, whoever asks; only the reporting status may advance and the links to a removed booking or customer may be cleared. Corrections must be new documents (credit notes): which documents and when is the open legal question on refund-and-cancellation-documents-for-issued-tax-invoices-are-undefined. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate, reproduced: as an administrator, 'update invoices set total_amount_sar = 1, vat_amount_sar = 0' and 'delete from invoices' both succeed and add no admin_audit_logs row. The technical control (an issued invoice is append-only; corrections are a new credit note) does not depend on the open ZATCA retention and PDPL interpretation, which stays with the owner. REMEDY: replace the FOR ALL policy with SELECT only for administrators, add a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that refuses changes to an issued invoice, and issue corrections as new rows.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): administrators can only read invoices (a forged insert is refused 42501); edits and deletes are refused for administrator, owner, customer, visitor and the service role; deleting the booking or the customer clears the link without touching the figures; the reporting status can advance; deleting a provider that has invoices is refused (a deliberate consequence of keeping tax records: a provider with issued invoices can never be removed). Dropping the protection trigger fails three tests.

gaps.description: admin_create_refund_request builds its idempotency key from the booking id plus a new UUID generated on every call, so the key can never repeat. A double click, a retried request after a lost response, or two operators acting on the same ticket each create a separate pending refund request; process-refund then sends each to the payment gateway under its own idempotency key. The cap against the captured amount stops an over-refund of the whole payment but not a doubled partial refund.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): the idempotency key is derived from the booking, the amount and the reason (or supplied by the caller), so a replay returns the existing request; a separate refund of the same size needs its own key. Proven by the replay test. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate, reproduced: two identical calls admin_create_refund_request(booking, 5, 'Goodwill refund') returned two different ids and left two pending refund_requests of 5.00 each. The money-command rule (verification and security references) requires one effect per replay. REMEDY: derive the key from (booking, amount, reason) or accept a client-supplied idempotency key like admin_release_payout does, and return the existing request when the key repeats; move the case in the repro file into the suite when fixed. The console does not call this command yet, so it is also a trap for the first screen that does.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): two identical calls return the same request and one refund row; a different letter case of the reason is the same request. Residual by design: retrying with an edited reason creates a second pending refund of the same amount unless the caller supplies the same idempotency key, so a screen that adds this command must send a stable key per refund decision.

gaps.description: supabase/functions/process-payout is a second, older way to pay out that no screen calls any more (the ledger screen uses admin_release_payout). It is still in the repository and deployable. Called with status 'paid' by any administrator token it releases whole pending ledger rows until their provider_share reaches the amount (so it can release more than was requested and ignores partial payout_allocations), never checks that the ledger covers the request, then marks the request paid. It writes with the service key, so the row-level audit trigger skips it, and it calls no audit writer, takes no reason, and has no idempotency key.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): process-payout and request-payout keep their administrator or signed-in gate and now answer 410 Gone without touching the ledger or payout requests; payouts are reviewed and released only through admin_review_payout_request and admin_release_payout. Deno cannot run here, so the deployed behaviour is unverified; deploying these two files replaces the live functions. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate by reading the function (Deno cannot run here, so runtime behaviour is unverified): lines 112-146 select pending rows by bookings.branches.provider_id and update payout_status to released; line 153 updates the request with no check that coveredAmount reached targetAmount. It is a privileged path with no control surface and no audit event. REMEDY: delete the function and its deployment, or reduce it to a thin caller of admin_release_payout; request-payout is the same class (it duplicates request_provider_payout without the IBAN and amount checks) and should go with it.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): process-payout answers 410 after its administrator gate and request-payout answers 410 after authentication; neither reaches a ledger or payout write (source read; Deno cannot run here, so runtime behaviour is unverified). The CORS origin matching in both is a separate open gap.

gaps.description: The Ledger screen was not part of the dialog migration. Releasing a provider's share for a ledger entry (admin_release_ledger_item) asks a window.confirm with the amount and nothing else: no reason, no target beyond the amount, no typed confirmation, and the command itself has no reason argument. Payout review and 'mark paid' use window.prompt (the paid step is a typed amount), and the release note sent to admin_release_payout is a fixed sentence the screen writes itself. Dispute arbitration and review moderation also use window.prompt; the services, branches, coupons and integrations screens use window.confirm. Native dialogs cannot name the record, are not announced consistently, and a refused command loses what the operator typed.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): admin_release_ledger_item and admin_release_payout now require a reason of at least three characters and record it; the ledger releases, payout review, payout paid (the amount must be typed), dispute decisions, review moderation, payment-method changes, application approval and the deactivate and archive confirmations all use the shared dialog that names the target. No native prompt or confirm remains under the admin screens (a test enforces it). PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate by reading the screens and calling the commands. These are the highest-value commands in the console (settling provider money), they sit outside the CommandDialog the other screens now use, and the audit entry for ledger.manually_settled carries no reason. REMEDY: move ledger release, payout review and release, dispute resolution and review moderation onto CommandDialog with a required reason; add a reason argument (minimum three characters, like the other reasoned commands) to admin_release_ledger_item and admin_release_payout and take the audit detail from it.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): in the browser the mark-paid dialog names the request, provider, amount and masked bank, needs a reason and the typed amount, keeps both after a refused command and sends p_reason with a stable idempotency key; the reject dialog names the request and needs a reason; the release, review and pay commands refuse a missing or short reason at the database. NOT exercised: the release-item dialog, disputes and review moderation (the stand-in does not serve them; the code opens CommandDialog and its rpc parameter names match the database signatures). The provider registration review still uses bare prompt() calls: provider-registration-review-still-asks-through-bare-native-prompts.

gaps.description: set_user_role(user, role) is the only way to make or remove an administrator. It has no console screen and no capability in the manifest, takes no reason, needs no second approver, and has no guard against removing the last administrator or oneself. Granting admin is recorded by the row audit trigger (role before and after, no reason). Demoting yourself is not recorded at all, because the trigger decides 'operator action' from is_admin() after the update has already removed the role. Removing the last administrator leaves nobody able to run the console.
gaps.rationale: PARTLY FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): set_user_role needs a reason, refuses to change the caller's own role, refuses to remove the last administrator, serializes concurrent changes and writes an audit entry with the roles before and after and the reason (a demotion by direct write is recorded too). STILL OPEN: there is still no console screen for granting or revoking the administrator role, and no second approver or recent re-authentication: who may grant administrator access and how it is approved are owner decisions (see admin-sessions-have-no-mfa-or-step-up and no-separation-of-duties). PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate, reproduced: an administrator promoted a customer to admin (one audit row, no reason), demoted another administrator (audited), and as the only administrator demoted themself with set_user_role (accepted, zero administrators left, no audit row). Access grants are a high-risk command class that needs reason capture, an audit entry in every case and a last-administrator guard. REMEDY: give role administration a screen and a reasoned command (reason, never the last admin, always audited, ideally second approver and recent re-authentication per admin-sessions-have-no-mfa-or-step-up) and revoke direct EXECUTE on set_user_role.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): the command part is closed: a reason of three characters, never the caller's own role, a last-administrator check inside an advisory lock, an audit entry with before, after and the reason, no overload without a reason, and a direct profile role write is refused. The remaining part (no screen, no second approver) is described honestly above and stays open.

gaps.description: employee_time_off has a SELECT policy that lets any authenticated user read every approved row, including the free-text reason column. A staff member who writes 'Chemotherapy appointment' or 'family bereavement' exposes it to every customer and every competing provider that has an account (accounts are free to create). Availability needs the dates, not the reason.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): only the staff member, the provider's owner and administrators read employee_time_off now, and get_available_slots runs with the definer's rights so a day off still removes the slots (tested). Side effect to review: slots now also exclude other customers' bookings for a customer caller, as the booking itself always did. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate, reproduced: another customer selecting reason from employee_time_off received the reason of an approved leave row; an anonymous visitor received nothing. Health and family details of staff are personal data under PDPL. REMEDY: expose availability through a view or the slot functions with start and end dates only, and restrict the base table to the employee, the provider owner and administrators; leave the reason out of anything a customer can query.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): only the staff member, the owner and administrators read employee_time_off; customers, visitors, other owners read 0 rows; an approved day off still removes the slots and create_booking is refused on that slot (including 'any available'); a pending request blocks nothing. Re-adding the old policy fails the test. Residual: a delegated manager cannot read the table, and the leave reason is copied into the audit log when an administrator edits it (audit-redaction-is-a-short-deny-list).

gaps.description: cancel_booking, mark_booking_no_show and employee_update_booking_status (the commands behind the Bookings screen's cancel, no-show and complete actions, and the cancellation that triggers a refund) accept a null, empty, whitespace or one-character reason when an administrator calls them directly. The nine newer reasoned commands refuse anything under three characters at the database. The reason rule for bookings lives only in the dialog on the screen.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): cancel_booking, mark_booking_no_show and employee_update_booking_status refuse an administrator's reason shorter than three characters (the booking dialog now requires one for completing too), and change nothing when they refuse. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate, reproduced: admin calls with reason null, '', '   ' and 'x' all returned success for the three commands. Reason capture is a server-side safeguard for financial and moderation actions; a screen check is not. Also inconsistent: admin_create_refund_request, moderate_review and reject_provider_application refuse blank reasons but accept one or two characters. REMEDY: one shared reason check (trimmed length at least three) used by every reasoned command, and a test over the catalog like the one in the suite for the nine commands.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): administrator calls of cancel_booking, mark_booking_no_show and employee_update_booking_status with null, empty, blank, 1 and 2 character reasons are refused 22023, three characters are accepted, and a provider's own owner is not forced to give one. Removing the check fails the test. Other commands still accept a one character reason: reason-length-rules-differ-across-administrator-commands.

gaps.description: get_booking_address_secure (home-service address reveal, 'G37') reads v_booking.client_id and employees.user_id, neither of which exists (bookings has customer_id, employees has profile_id). Every call, from the customer, the provider owner, an employee or an administrator, ends in SQLSTATE 42703 'record v_booking has no field client_id'. The feature never worked, and no screen calls it yet. The test that covers it reads the migration text and passes.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): the function read columns that do not exist (client_id, employees.user_id, branches.address_ar) and an enum value that does not exist (in_service); it now answers the booking's customer, staff, provider owner and administrators, and a stranger as if the booking did not exist. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate, reproduced: the booking's own customer, the provider owner and an administrator each received 42703. The authorization the function intends (customer, assigned specialist, owner, admin) is therefore untested, and the address privacy rule is unverified. REMEDY: correct the column names, call the function from the provider screens that need the address, and test it by role (own customer, assigned employee, other customer, other provider, anonymous) against the schema.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): the booking's customer, the owner, the assigned employee and an administrator receive the address of a confirmed home visit, a masked notice while it is pending and the branch address for a salon visit; another customer and another owner receive P0002; a visitor 42501.

gaps.description: web_platform/tests/negative-authorization.test.mjs (1,348 lines, cited as policy-test evidence) never connects to a database or calls a function. Its cases read one SQL or TypeScript file and assert that a string such as IF COALESCE(auth.jwt()->>'role', '') <> 'service_role' appears. Such a test passes when a later migration replaces the guarded function with an unguarded one, passes for a function that fails on every call (get_booking_address_secure), and says nothing about row policies. Only the PGlite suites under supabase/tests/db execute the boundary.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate by reading the suite and comparing it with executing tests. Source-text assertions are acceptable as a cheap guard against edge-function regressions (the Deno functions cannot run here) but must not stand as role-by-operation evidence for database commands. REMEDY: keep them, rename them as source guards, and cite the executing suites (supabase/tests/db/admin_security_matrix.test.mjs and qa_adversarial.test.mjs) for each capability's authorization policy tests; extend the executing matrix to the commands that only the text tests cover (the owner commands for payouts, reviews, packages, coupons).

gaps.description: supabase/functions/calculate-travel reads no Authorization header and checks no identity. Anyone who holds the public project key (it ships in every browser bundle) can post coordinates and each call is forwarded to the Google Distance Matrix API under the project's GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, which is billed per request. There is no rate limit or quota guard. It returns Google's raw error text to the caller on failure.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): the function now needs a signed-in session (getUser on the bearer token, 401 otherwise) before it reads the Maps key, and refuses coordinates that are not numbers in range. Nothing in the web or mobile code calls it. Deno cannot run here, so the deployed behaviour is unverified. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate by reading the function (Deno cannot run here; runtime behaviour unverified). It holds no service-role key, so this is a cost and availability exposure rather than a data one. REMEDY: require a signed-in user (resolveCaller from _shared/http.ts), validate the coordinates (range, numeric), cap calls per user per minute, and return a generic error.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): source read: a session token is required and checked with getUser, coordinates are validated for range; Deno cannot run here so runtime behaviour is unverified. Residual: any signed-in account (free to create) can still spend the Maps quota, there is no per-user rate limit, and the function still returns Google's raw error text; the screens do not call it. The origin matching is covered by the open CORS gap.

gaps.description: Edge functions that act with the service key write through a path the row audit trigger skips (it ignores service_role) and most call no audit writer. expire-holds lets an administrator choose hold_interval_minutes (any positive number, so 0.01 expires live pending-payment bookings that customers are still paying) and records nothing about who ran it or why; the audited console command admin_release_expired_holds has no such parameter. send-notification lets an administrator push any title and body to any user's devices with no record. process-refund executes as the service key with no operator in the audit trail (gap refund-execution-has-no-operator-in-the-audit-trail).
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate by reading the functions (Deno cannot run here). The same operator action done through the console is audited with actor and reason; done through these functions it is not, so the audit trail depends on which door was used. REMEDY: have each function record the authenticated caller, the request and the result through a service-role audit writer (write_audit_log with the caller id passed in), reject a caller-supplied hold interval, and give admin push messages the same reasoned, audited command as admin_broadcast_notification.

gaps.description: calculate-travel, process-payout, request-payout, send-notification, send-otp and send-push reflect the request Origin whenever it ends in .vercel.app or in primora.sa. Any project anyone deploys on Vercel, and any host such as evilprimora.sa, is therefore allowed to call these functions from a browser. The functions authenticate with a bearer token, not cookies, so this does not by itself give an attacker access, but it removes the browser's second line of defence for the two money functions.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate by reading the functions. The shared helper _shared/http.ts used by the newer functions has an exact allow-list; the older functions still carry their own copies. REMEDY: replace the endsWith checks with the exact list in _shared/http.ts and delete the local copies.

gaps.description: cancel_booking and the other booking commands answer a booking that exists but belongs to someone else with 42501 'Not authorized' and a missing booking with P0002 'Booking not found'. A caller holding a candidate id learns whether it exists. Ids are UUIDs, so guessing is impractical and the exposure is small.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3b, unreviewed): reschedule_booking (which now checks who the caller is before it looks at the status), customer_confirm_attendance and generate_zatca_tax_invoice join the other booking commands in answering a stranger exactly like a missing booking. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: RE-OPENED BY qa-claude-release-gate (round 3, 2026-10-06): four of the seven commands now answer a foreign booking like a missing one (cancel_booking, mark_booking_no_show, employee_update_booking_status, get_booking_address_secure: verified in the executing suite) but reschedule_booking ('Not authorized to reschedule this booking' against 'Booking not found'), customer_confirm_attendance and generate_zatca_tax_invoice ('Not authorized to view this invoice') still tell the caller whether the id exists. Reproduced as another customer. open_booking_dispute and add_booking_tip already answer both cases alike. REMEDY: the same one-line change in the three remaining functions.  PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): the three booking commands and the address function answer a booking the caller has no part in exactly as they answer a missing one (P0002, 'Booking not found'). PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate, reproduced (QA-8). Verification rule: a refusal should not distinguish forbidden from missing where that leaks existence. REMEDY: answer both cases identically for callers who are not staff of the booking.  QA-VERIFIED round 4 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing against the migrated schema): reschedule_booking, customer_confirm_attendance and generate_zatca_tax_invoice answer another customer and another provider's owner exactly as they answer a missing id, and the owner's own reschedule still works.

gaps.description: Anyone, signed in or not, can read every WhatsApp message template (14 rows of operational copy) and every platform_settings row, including approved_by (the identifier of the administrator who approved the last change to a setting that requires owner approval). The templates are the company's outbound wording; the approver id is internal.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate in the anonymous read sweep (suite test 'shows an anonymous visitor only the public catalogue', which lists both tables as accepted public reads until this is decided). REMEDY: if the booking pages need only the hold minutes and loyalty switch, expose those through a view or function and restrict the base tables to signed-in staff.

gaps.description: At phone width, switching language from the header without reloading leaves the closed (inert) navigation drawer 87 px inside the viewport: the class list is correct (right-0 translate-x-full) but the computed translate stays at the previous language's value (-100%), so the drawer's edge covers the side of the page. A reload fixes it.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate in the Browser pane's Chromium against the verification stand-in: LTR load, drawer x=-288; click the Arabic switch, drawer x=-201 and still -201 after 3 s; reload, x=375. Cosmetic and not data-affecting; other browsers not tried. REMEDY: key the drawer on the direction so it remounts, or drive the offset with logical properties (inset-inline-start, translate with the direction variable).

gaps.description: The Packages and Services screens start their language state as Arabic and build their error text when the request fails, so an English operator sees 'تعذر تحميل الباقات من قاعدة البيانات.' and 'فشل ت...' on a failed load. Both screens are outside the ten reviewed screens. The repository rule is that no UI string may ignore the active locale.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate in the browser with the stand-in refusing the table (English interface, Arabic error). REMEDY: derive the language from the shell's locale hook (useOperationsLocale) instead of local state defaulting to ar.

gaps.description: The Bookings screen filters by status only and lists the newest 500 bookings for that filter. There is no search by booking id, invoice number, customer name or phone, provider or date range, and no page beyond 500, so a dispute, refund or PDPL request about a booking from four months ago cannot be located without engineering (SQL). Totals on the screen cover the listed rows only (the screen says so honestly). The find step of the completeness test fails for the most common support lookup.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): the Bookings screen reads admin_booking_directory: search by booking ID, invoice number, customer or provider, status and Riyadh date range, 25 per page (clamped to 100), totals over every matching booking, each listing audited without the search text. The filters live in the address bar. Checked in a browser against the stand-in API: 1,420 bookings reachable, a date range after its end refused. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate in the browser (1,420 bookings in the stand-in, 500 rendered) and in the code (limit 500, one status filter). Related to the open no-pagination-or-server-side-filtering, which is generic; this records the specific operator workflow that cannot be completed. REMEDY: a paginated admin_booking_directory command (search, date range, status, provider; clamped page size; each listing audited like admin_customer_overview) and the same filters in the address bar.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): admin_booking_directory is administrator-only, clamps the page to 100 and offsets to zero, finds a booking by id, invoice number, customer or provider, cuts a Riyadh day at Riyadh midnight, treats percent, underscores, quotes, long text and partial ids as plain text, rejects an unknown status and an inverted range, and audits every call without the search text. In the browser: search, paging with focus kept on Next, 'Showing 26-50 of 111', totals over all matches, an inverted date range refused with a named message and no request.

gaps.description: wallet_credits, gift_cards, gift_card_redemptions, customer_loyalty and loyalty_points_ledger are administrator-writable tables with audit triggers, but no admin screen shows or adjusts them. A support agent who must look up a customer's wallet, void a gift card or give a goodwill credit has no controlled way to do it, so it is done with SQL or a direct table write that carries no reason.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate by comparing customer-facing money features with administrative obligations (customer wallet, gift cards and loyalty exist in the apps and migrations; the console has nothing). Per-entity review: list and search, detail with ledger history, reasoned credit and debit commands with limits, void for gift cards, audit. No business decision is needed to build the read side; limits on adjustments are an owner decision.

gaps.description: platform_feature_flags (including payments_marketplace_split, which makes payment-checkout refuse every charge when switched on), fee_rules (the commission and VAT rates every booking is priced with; the Taxes screen shows them read-only), subscription_plans and provider_subscriptions (what providers pay for plans, and whether a payment is pending) have no screen and no command. Changing any of them means a migration or SQL by an engineer.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate by searching the console for each table. Changing commission or VAT rates is an owner decision (AGENTS.md); a controlled way to do it (reasoned, audited, second approver) is still an operator need, and the read side for flags and plan subscriptions needs no decision. The capabilities settings.vat-rate and settings.commission are discovered but unbuilt.

gaps.description: admin_publish_agreement and admin_record_cr_review exist as commands; only the second has a screen. Publishing a new terms or privacy version (which drives consent re-acceptance) and viewing who has accepted which version has no console surface, so it is done outside the console.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate (grep over app/admin for the command and the legal_agreements and agreement_acceptances tables). Which text to publish is legal; a reasoned, audited publish command with a version list and an acceptance count is an operator need.

gaps.description: Customers post jobs that every provider can read and bid on (job_posts, job_bids), and customers and providers exchange messages (conversations, messages). Reviews can be moderated; neither of these can: an abusive post, a scam message or a report about a provider has no administrator queue, hide action or audit.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate comparing the customer-facing features with the console. Message content is personal data, so access needs a reason and an audit entry (privileged read), which is why this is an owner decision about scope as much as a build task.

gaps.description: The platform issues ZATCA tax invoices (generate_zatca_tax_invoice) and refunds money (refund_requests, process-refund), but nothing links a refund or cancellation to the invoice it reverses: no credit note, no adjusted VAT figure, no report line. Whether a credit note is required, and for which amounts, is a tax-law interpretation.
gaps.rationale: BLOCKED ON OWNER/LEGAL DECISION (qa-claude-release-gate): AGENTS.md reserves ZATCA interpretation for a human. The decision needed: which refunds and cancellations require a credit note, who issues it, and how the VAT summary report treats them. Until then the VAT figures the console shows are gross of refunds.

gaps.description: ledger.release-payout, ledger.mark-refunded, payout.approve and payout.mark-paid are still at status discovered with notes that describe the old code ('writes payout_status=released straight from the browser, no idempotency key, no audit event'). The screens now call admin_release_ledger_item, admin_review_payout_request and admin_release_payout, which have tests. The manifest therefore reports the highest-risk workflows as unbuilt and untested while the code and the executing suites say otherwise, and the 94 release-status errors hide which of them are real.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3, unreviewed): ledger.release-payout, payout.approve and payout.mark-paid now name their server operations, policies, audit events, tests and evidence and are marked implemented (unreviewed). PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate comparing the manifest with the code. Verification honesty: a capability record must describe the system as built, with its tests and evidence, or it cannot be reviewed. REMEDY (implementer pass): update each capability with its real server operation, policy tests (supabase/tests/db/qa_adversarial.test.mjs replay and reason cases, admin_security_matrix.test.mjs) and screen, then mark implemented for review; the open findings above stay open on their own gaps.  QA-VERIFIED round 3 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing suites and stand-in browser; hosted project not contacted): ledger.release-payout, payout.approve and payout.mark-paid now name their server operations, tests, safeguards and audit events and are reviewed (see their review status). The four siblings are tracked in ledger-and-payout-sibling-capabilities-keep-pre-fix-notes.

gaps.description: The Audit Log screen filters, pages and expands entries but cannot export a filtered period for an external auditor, and no retention rule says how long admin_audit_logs rows are kept or who may purge them (the table has no delete path for client roles, and nothing else is defined). integration_audit_log, the second audit table, has no screen.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate in the per-entity review (audit history: list and search yes; export, retention, archive no). Retention length is a legal decision; an audited export of the audit log itself (an export of an export record) is not.

gaps.description: With the audit trigger on every table, a set-based administrator write is recorded row by row: an administrator-session insert of 4,000 rows into notifications took 452 ms and wrote 4,000 audit rows (3.7 MB); the service role does the same in 64 ms and writes none. An administrator broadcast (admin_broadcast_notification) therefore writes one audit row for every recipient's notification and every queued WhatsApp message on top of its own single 'notification.broadcast' entry, and every cancellation or completion writes ten or so. The log the Audit screen pages through fills with machine-made rows, hiding the operator actions it exists to show, and a broadcast to a large audience is slowed several-fold.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3b, unreviewed): the first five audited row changes in a transaction are itemised, then one summary row says the rest were not itemised (the command that caused them keeps its own entry); a 500-row administrator statement writes six rows. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate (round 3), measured against the migrated schema. The trigger is FOR EACH ROW and builds the before and after documents (to_jsonb) for every row before it knows whether the session is an administrator's. REMEDY: record one summary row per statement for writes made inside a console command (a statement-level trigger with transition tables, or the command's own audit entry only), keep row-level capture for direct table writes, and have the early exit run before the to_jsonb calls.  QA-VERIFIED round 4 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing against the migrated schema): a 500-row administrator insert writes 6 audit rows (5 itemised and a bulk_write summary) and a 500-row delete writes 6; the early exit for non-administrators and the service role is unchanged. Residual, accepted by design: the counter is per transaction across tables, so inside one command that writes many rows the later row changes are not itemised (the command writes its own audit entry), and an audit reason set by one command stays attached to a later write in the same transaction; neither is reachable from separate requests.

gaps.description: Recording a provider's commercial registration (CR) review, a compliance command (admin_record_cr_review), still collects its input with two bare browser prompt() calls: the CR number, then 'What did you check?'. The 'Check with Wathq' action asks for the CR number the same way. The guard test that is meant to keep native dialogs out of the admin screens matches only window.prompt( and window.confirm(, so these three calls pass it, and the implementer's statement that no native prompt is left under app/admin is wrong.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3b, unreviewed): the Wathq check and the manual Commercial Registration review use the shared dialog with a validated 10-digit field and, for the manual review, a required note; the guard now also catches bare prompt, confirm and alert calls, not only the window-prefixed ones. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate (round 3) by searching the source for prompt( without a window prefix. The same defects as the ones fixed on the other screens apply: the dialog cannot name the provider, a refusal loses what was typed, there is no minimum for the note, and a CR number typed into a prompt is not validated before the command is sent. REMEDY: move both actions onto CommandDialog with a CR number field and a required note, and widen the guard to /(^|[^.\w])(prompt|confirm|alert)\(/ as well as the window forms.  QA-VERIFIED round 4 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing against the migrated schema): no bare prompt( remains in provider-management.tsx; the CR number and the review note go through CommandDialog with a field; the guard now matches bare, window-qualified and alert forms. Not opened in a browser this round (source read).

gaps.description: Nine reasoned administrator commands and the three booking commands now refuse a reason shorter than three characters. moderate_review, reject_provider_application and resolve_booking_dispute still refuse only a blank one and accept 'x'. The screens enforce three characters, so the difference shows only to a caller that bypasses them.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3b, unreviewed): moderate_review (hidden and flagged), reject_provider_application and resolve_booking_dispute now refuse a reason shorter than three characters like every other reasoned command. PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate (round 3); reproduced by calling each with a one character reason, which goes on to look up the record instead of being refused. REMEDY: one shared reason check (trimmed length of at least three) used by every reasoned command, with a catalog-driven test over every function that takes a reason argument.  QA-VERIFIED round 4 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing against the migrated schema): moderate_review (hidden and flagged), reject_provider_application and resolve_booking_dispute refuse a one-character reason with 22023; publishing a review still needs no reason.

gaps.description: The one remaining policy on employee_time_off ('Employees request own time off and owners manage', FOR ALL) lets a staff member insert or update their own row with status 'approved'. A request that is meant to wait for the owner can approve itself and remove the staff member's slots from sale.
gaps.rationale: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 4, unreviewed): the trigger now also refuses a staff member's change of the dates or the person on leave that is already approved; only the owner, a delegate with the staff permission, an administrator or the system make those changes. (A delegate reading leave through the table policy is a separate, unchanged matter.) PREVIOUS RATIONALE: RE-OPENED BY qa-claude-release-gate (round 4, 2026-10-06): the trigger refuses an approved row from the staff member (insert, and pending to approved) and lets the owner, administrators and the service role through, but it acts only on a change of status. A staff member can still edit the dates of a row the owner already approved (status stays approved) and widen it to 30 days, which removes their slots from sale without the owner's say. A delegate with the staff permission is allowed by the trigger but the table policy gives them no rows. REMEDY: refuse any change to start_date, end_date or employee_id by a non-approver once the row is approved (or return it to pending), and add delegates to the policy.  PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FIXED IN SOURCE (impl-claude-release-gaps, 2026-10-06, round 3b, unreviewed): a trigger refuses a staff member's insert or update that sets leave to approved; the provider's owner, a delegate with the staff permission, an administrator and the system still can. A staff member can still ask (pending). PREVIOUS RATIONALE: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate (round 3): a provider employee inserted an approved leave row for their own employee id and it was accepted. Not new (the policy is older than this work) but it now matters, because an approved row alone decides whether customers can book. REMEDY: split the policy so staff may insert and cancel their own rows only as 'pending', and only the owner, a delegate with the staff permission and administrators set 'approved' or 'rejected'; give delegates read access to the table.  QA-VERIFIED round 5 (qa-claude-release-gate, 2026-10-06, executing against the migrated schema): widening the dates of an approved row or moving it to another employee is refused for the staff member; their own pending row, a reason-only edit, and the owner, administrator and service role are unaffected; another provider's owner changes 0 rows. A delegate with the staff permission still sees no rows because the table policy omits delegates (not a trigger problem).

gaps.description: After round 3 the capabilities ledger.release-payout, payout.approve and payout.mark-paid describe the built commands, but their siblings ledger.list, ledger.vat-report, payout.list and payout.reject are still at status discovered with notes that describe the old code ('substitutes invented VAT totals', 'the admin_note is a hardcoded English string'). The screen no longer does either: a failed VAT report load is shown as an error and a payout rejection takes a reason in a dialog. payout.reject is the same command as payout.approve and has tests. The manifest therefore still under-reports the ledger domain and its 94 release-status errors hide which are real.
gaps.rationale: FOUND BY qa-claude-release-gate (round 3) comparing the capability notes with the source. REMEDY (implementer pass): update the four capabilities with their real server operation, tests and evidence, mark them implemented, and leave ledger.mark-refunded discovered (it is accurate: no console surface writes a refunded status).

declaredStatic.reason: Reversible catalog states defined by the database schema, rather than operational sample data.
declaredStatic.approvedBy: User-approved P3 scope and delegated implementation choices

feedback.observation: In audit mode the architect must record a verdict per capability (real / decorative / missing / silently-failing) but the capability status enum only expresses build progress, so the verdict has to be smuggled into the rationale prose. The manifest cannot then be queried for 'show me every decorative screen'.
feedback.proposedChange: Add an optional capability field such as auditVerdict with an enum of live, partial, decorative, missing, silently-failing, and teach `report` and `coverage` to summarise by it.

feedback.observation: The single most damaging pattern found in this codebase was a catch block whose body is identical to the try block, so every failure reports success. It defeats RLS observability, hides unapplied migrations and makes a decorative screen indistinguishable from a working one. It is not named in capability-catalog.md or verification.md.
feedback.proposedChange: Add 'catch-and-succeed' to the anti-pattern list in capability-catalog.md, and add a grep-based check to verification.md: a catch block that calls the same success setter as its try block is a defect.

feedback.observation: Several screens substitute demo data when a query returns ZERO ROWS rather than when it errors. This is more dangerous than an error fallback because it fires in normal operation on a quiet month - a VAT screen showed invented tax totals this way. The discovery reference warns about placeholder data but not about this specific trigger.
feedback.proposedChange: In discovery.md and verification.md, state explicitly that a zero-row result must render an empty state and never substitute sample data, and call out financial and compliance screens as absolute.

feedback.observation: Supabase Edge Functions default to verify_jwt=true, which developers read as 'authenticated', but the check is satisfied by the project's public publishable/anon key that ships in every browser bundle. Two service-role functions here relied on it and had no role check of their own. stack-adapters.md does not warn about this.
feedback.proposedChange: Add to the Supabase section of stack-adapters.md: verify_jwt is not authorization; every service-role Edge Function must independently call auth.getUser on the bearer token and check the role, and Access-Control-Allow-Origin should not be '*' on a privileged function.

feedback.observation: The most consequential question in this audit - which migrations are applied to the live project - was unanswerable because the Supabase MCP server was unauthenticated in a non-interactive session. Roughly a third of the security findings had to be stated conditionally.
feedback.proposedChange: Have the audit agent check for live-database reachability at the START of the pass and, when it is missing, say so in the first paragraph of the report and list precisely which findings are conditional on it, rather than discovering the limitation midway.

feedback.observation: A newer local Claude reference added a migration with the initial P3 timestamp. Read-only reconciliation caught the collision before deployment.
feedback.suggestedChange: Inspect all visible branch migration versions before numbering an additive migration and exercise the full target chain in isolated Postgres.

feedback.observation: placeholder-scan rejects any tests[] entry whose path contains 'mock', so the release-path guard web_platform/tests/no-mock-data.test.mjs cannot be cited as a screen or capability test.
feedback.proposedChange: Skip placeholder-scan for tests[] and evidence[] paths that exist on disk, or match tokens only inside quoted values rather than file names.

feedback.observation: The refund-request entity was modelled on payment_refund_requests, which nothing writes any more; the live queue (refund_requests, added by a later migration) had no screen and refunds that exhausted automatic retries were invisible.
feedback.proposedChange: Architect pass: for each entity's sourceOfTruth, confirm a current migration or function still INSERTs into it; when a newer table supersedes it, model the newer one.

feedback.observation: With Tailwind 4, an unlayered global rule (.primora-dashboard-skin > aside { position: relative }) overrode the layered 'fixed' and 'z-50' utilities, so the admin phone drawer stayed in the page flow and pushed every screen 1,300 px down. Desktop review could not see it.
feedback.proposedChange: UX review at phone width: check the computed position of every fixed overlay and the top offset of main content; flag unlayered global selectors that target layout elements.

feedback.observation: A PDPL 'anonymize' action wrote Math.random-based phone numbers into a UNIQUE column, colliding between erasures and able to take a real person's number, and discarded the operator's reason.
feedback.proposedChange: Add Math.random (and Date.now-derived identifiers) inside write payloads to the placeholder scan for operator screens; require PII clearing to be one audited server command that writes NULL, not invented values.

feedback.observation: emit --format authz-matrix is derived from the manifest alone, so a privileged function that was never modelled (several admin_* commands were absent until late) or a role-by-table direct write never appears in it; 40 of 70 rows showed no policy. The strongest evidence in this review was a test that enumerates admin-gated functions from pg_proc and calls each as every non-admin role.
feedback.proposedChange: In security-governance.md and verification.md, add a catalog-driven check for stacks with a queryable catalog: list privileged functions and admin-writable tables from the database and diff them against the manifest, and run each as every role expecting an authorization error before any validation error.

feedback.observation: An audit trigger was attached to the eleven tables the console's screens write, while 13 other tables kept FOR ALL admin RLS policies with no trigger, including the ledger, wallet credits and fee rules. 'Every console write is audited' was true of the screens and false of the credential.
feedback.proposedChange: In stack-adapters.md (Supabase), derive the audit-trigger table list from pg_policies (admin policies that allow writes), not from the screens, and require admin-writable money tables to be append-only or command-only.

feedback.observation: The audit decision 'rls-is-sound' and the guidance that RLS is the authorization boundary held for rows but not for columns: public row policies with default column grants exposed admin_notes, Wathq data and staff phone numbers to anonymous callers.
feedback.proposedChange: In stack-adapters.md (Supabase), state that row policies do not restrict columns; every table with a public or broad read policy needs a column-grant or view review for internal fields.

feedback.observation: A deny-list of seven column names was used to keep secrets out of a row-level audit trigger; a PDPL clear command then wrote the cleared name and push token into the append-only log, and the test only checked the phone column.
feedback.proposedChange: In security-governance.md (Audit records), require allow-listed audit columns per table and a test that runs the command's own sensitive fixture through the audit and asserts none of its values appear.

feedback.observation: The security role is told to hold the claim while writing crossCutting, but claim accepts only capability ids, so there is nothing to claim for that section; the only protection is the per-write lock. reviewStatus can also be set on in-progress capabilities although the release rule checks implemented ones, which left it unclear whether a reviewer should wait.
feedback.proposedChange: Let claim take a section name such as crossCutting, and state in multi-agent.md whether reviewStatus may be set before status is implemented.

feedback.observation: Five of the migrations that define the most important policies (harden_auth_and_booking_core, review_fix_booking_core, review_fix_money, review_fix_trust_growth, phone_identity_and_consents) are rejected as evidence by the placeholder content scan because they contain ordinary words such as sample or random, so security evidence had to cite newer files or test files instead of the policy source.
feedback.proposedChange: Scan only manifest-authored text and file names, not the content of cited source files, or let a cited path#Lnn range scope the scan to those lines.

feedback.observation: A reviewer is told to claim the capabilities it reviews, but claim writes capabilities[].owner (the field the reviewer-identity rule compares with reviewedBy) and takes an exclusive lock, so the UX and security reviewers that the multi-agent guide says run in parallel over one domain cannot both hold the same capability.
feedback.proposedChange: Give reviewers a non-exclusive review marker (agents[].reviewing[]) instead of the implementer claim, and keep owner for the implementer only.

feedback.observation: The ux-reviewer contract asks for accessibilityStatus 'with an evidence path', but the screen schema holds only an enum and a single rationale owned by the implementer, so reviewer evidence has nowhere to live except a worklog.
feedback.proposedChange: Add screens[].reviewEvidence[] (paths) and screens[].reviewedBy so a UX pass can attach its checks without overwriting the implementer's rationale.

feedback.observation: A scripted focus sweep (element.focus() on every control) reported nearly every control as having no focus indicator because :focus-visible does not match programmatic focus until a real key press has happened; the first run was a false alarm and only a run after a genuine Tab press was valid.
feedback.proposedChange: In verification.md, tell reviewers to send one real Tab key before any scripted focus sweep and to count controls where :focus-visible did not match, and ship the sweep snippet with the skill.
